OpenAI's 2024 friction between Sam Altman and Ilya Sutskever, Anthropic's stance that Claude is an assistant not a replacement, and Apple Intelligence's augment-not-replace pitch are all contemporary projections of a line drawn sixty years ago.
events.behind_scenes_en: Engelbart was proposing augmentation at SRI in the 1950s while McCarthy planned the AI discipline at Dartmouth. After brief early cooperation they parted ways: McCarthy moved from MIT to Stanford in 1962 and co-founded the Stanford AI Project with Minsky in 1963, and Engelbart founded SRI's Augmentation Research Center in 1963. Their laboratories sat less than ten miles apart, yet their ideas diverged so far that they barely cited each other. Only with the spread of personal computers in the late 1980s did the IA route win vindication in GUIs, hyperlinks, and wikis.

events.title_zh: RAND Tablet:低成本手写图形输入设备
events.title_en: RAND Tablet: Low-Cost Handwriting & Graphics Input
events.summary_zh:
1964 年,RAND 公司发布 RAND Tablet——一台造价约 18,000 美元的电子手写板,用网格状导线感应笔尖位置,分辨率 100 dpi,刷新率 100 次/秒。
相比同期 Lincoln Labs 的 Tablet，它造价相对低，第一次让普通实验室也能上手做笔输入实验。
MCI、SRI、RAND 的研究者用它做了大量手写识别、图形界面、签名验证研究。
events.source_name: Davis, M. R. & Ellis, T. O. (1964). RAND Tablet: A Man-Machine Graphical Communication Device. FJCC.
events.card_summary_zh: RAND Tablet：低成本手写图形输入设备；RAND Tablet 是后来 Apple Newton、Palm Pilot。
events.summary_en: In 1964, the RAND Corporation released the RAND Tablet, an electronic writing tablet costing about $18,000 that used a grid of wires to sense the stylus tip at a resolution of 100 dpi and a refresh rate of 100 times per second. Relatively cheaper than Lincoln Labs' contemporary tablet, it allowed ordinary labs to run pen-input experiments for the first time. Researchers at MCI, SRI, and RAND used it to conduct extensive studies on handwriting recognition, graphical interfaces, and signature verification.
events.card_summary_en: A low-cost pen-input tablet, ancestor of the Newton, Palm Pilot, Wacom, and iPad plus Pencil.
events.why_it_matters_en: The RAND Tablet is the ancestor of the whole pen-input plus recognition line running through Apple Newton, Palm Pilot, Wacom tablets, and iPad with Pencil. It turned writing on paper into a stream of signals a computer could capture for the first time, and online handwriting recognition stood up as a discipline branch from then on.
events.behind_scenes_en: The tablet was designed principally by M. R. Davis and T. O. Ellis, with the paper presented at the 1964 Fall Joint Computer Conference. Together with Engelbart's contemporaneous NLS mouse and Sutherland's Sketchpad of 1963, it formed the hardware foundation of human-computer interaction emerging as an independent direction in the 1960s. Yet mature pen input had to wait for the failure of Apple's Newton and the success of Palm in the 1990s, with three intervening decades dominated by mice and keyboards.

events.title_zh: DENDRAL 启动:第一个大型知识驱动专家系统
events.title_en: DENDRAL Project: First Knowledge-Intensive Expert System
events.summary_zh:
1965 年春,Edward Feigenbaum 刚加入 Stanford 任计算机系创始教员,立刻与诺奖遗传学家 Joshua Lederberg 启动 DENDRAL 项目,目标是让计算机从有机化合物的质谱图反推分子结构。
1966 年 Lederberg 拉入 Carl Djerassi(口服避孕药之父、Stanford 质谱实验室负责人)补齐化学知识。
项目持续到 1982,是史上第一个大型“知识库 + 推理机”专家系统。
核心思想——“程序的能力来自具体领域知识,而不是更聪明的推理”——被称为“知识原理”,1980 年代专家系统工业化的理论基石。
events.source_name: Lindsay, Buchanan, Feigenbaum, Lederberg (1993). DENDRAL: A case study. AI Journal 61:209-261.
events.card_summary_zh: DENDRAL 把化学家的经验写成可推理的规则，第一次证明 AI 能在狭窄但真实的专业领域超过普通人。
events.summary_en: In the spring of 1965, freshly appointed Stanford computer science founding faculty member Edward Feigenbaum partnered with Nobel laureate geneticist Joshua Lederberg to launch the DENDRAL project, aiming to make computers deduce molecular structures from the mass spectra of organic compounds. In 1966, Lederberg recruited Carl Djerassi—the father of the oral contraceptive pill and head of Stanford's mass spectrometry lab—to provide the crucial chemistry expertise. Running until 1982 as history's first large-scale "knowledge base + inference engine" expert system, its core philosophy that a program's power derives from domain-specific knowledge rather than smarter reasoning was dubbed the "knowledge principle," serving as the theoretical cornerstone for the industrialization of expert systems in the 1980s.
events.card_summary_en: It wrote chemists' expertise into rules, proving AI could beat novices in a narrow real domain.
events.why_it_matters_en: DENDRAL pulled AI from the dream of a universal reasoner down to the reality that domain knowledge is the key, directly spawning MYCIN, XCON, PROSPECTOR, and a generation of 1970s-80s expert systems. Feigenbaum became known as the father of expert systems and received the 1994 ACM Turing Award. Knowledge engineering as a profession began with DENDRAL, and today's prompt engineer is its distant descendant.
events.behind_scenes_en: The original design inspiration came from Lederberg's 1964 DENDRAL algorithm, a generator exhaustively enumerating all possible molecular structures. Exhaustion produces astronomical candidate structures, so chemists' heuristics had to prune them. Feigenbaum's key insight was to encode the chemists' experience directly into the program instead of simulating how scientists think. That trade of knowledge versus reasoning shaped the next twenty years of AI routes, and planted the seed of the expert-system bubble bursting in the late 1980s, since the knowledge-acquisition bottleneck remains unsolved.

events.title_zh: Ivakhnenko GMDH:第一个深度学习算法
events.title_en: Ivakhnenko's Group Method of Data Handling (GMDH)
events.summary_zh:
1965 年,乌克兰控制论学者 Alexey Ivakhnenko 与 Valentin Lapa 发表《Cybernetics and Forecasting Techniques》,提出 GMDH(Group Method of Data Handling,数据群处理法)——第一个能端到端训练深度前馈多层感知机的通用学习算法。
GMDH 用回归分析逐层增长网络,每层用单独验证集做剪枝,1971 年 Ivakhnenko 已实现 8 层深度网络——比西方“深度学习”概念早 30 多年。
events.source_name: Ivakhnenko, A. G. & Lapa, V. G. (1965). Cybernetics and Forecasting Techniques. Kiev: Naukova Dumka.
events.card_summary_zh: Ivakhnenko GMDH：第一个深度学习算法；GMDH 是“深度学习”真正的起点。
events.summary_en: In 1965, Ukrainian cyberneticians Alexey Ivakhnenko and Valentin Lapa published *Cybernetics and Forecasting Techniques*, introducing GMDH (Group Method of Data Handling)—the first general learning algorithm capable of training deep feedforward multilayer perceptrons end-to-end. By using regression analysis to grow the network layer by layer and pruning each layer with a separate validation set, Ivakhnenko had already implemented an 8-layer deep network by 1971, predating the Western concept of "deep learning" by more than 30 years.
events.card_summary_en: Ivakhnenko's GMDH is deep learning's true starting point, decades early and half a world away.
events.why_it_matters_en: GMDH is the real starting point of deep learning, and Schmidhuber accordingly calls Ivakhnenko the father of deep learning. Four years ahead of Minsky and Papert's pessimistic single-layer verdict in their 1969 Perceptrons, it proved that stacking layers to learn internal representations was already a walked path in the Soviet Union. Today's three essentials of deep learning, stacked layers, validation-set pruning, and internal representation learning, were all present in GMDH.
events.behind_scenes_en: Ivakhnenko worked at the Institute of Cybernetics of the Academy of Sciences of Ukraine in Kyiv and formally established the GMDH algorithmic system in 1968. Cold War language barriers confined his work to the Soviet Union and Eastern Europe until Japanese scholars introduced it to the West in 1971, and Farlow's 1980s English anthology brought wide recognition. After the Soviet collapse in 1989, GMDH was rediscovered in economic forecasting and ecological modeling. When the 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics went to Hinton and Hopfield, Schmidhuber publicly protested, calling it a Nobel prize for copying, and named Ivakhnenko in 1965, Amari in 1967, and Linnainmaa in 1970 as overlooked pioneers.

events.title_zh: Weizenbaum ELIZA:第一个聊天机器人的诞生
events.title_en: ELIZA: A Computer Program for the Study of Natural Language Communication
events.summary_zh:
1965 年,Joseph Weizenbaum 在 MIT Project MAC 用 MAD-SLIP 在 IBM 7094 上写出 ELIZA,通过 CTSS 分时系统让多个用户同时与程序对话。
ELIZA 是一个平台:换不同“脚本”就变不同角色。
最有名的脚本是 DOCTOR——模仿 Rogerian 心理治疗师,用“你刚才说...”“这让你想到什么?”等反问模板把用户的话包装成回应。
1966 年 1 月 CACM 9(1):36-45 发表,ELIZA 立刻成为史上第一个被普通用户当作“懂人话”的程序。
events.source_name: Weizenbaum, J. (1966). CACM 9(1):36-45
events.card_summary_zh: ELIZA 只靠简单规则复述用户的话，却让人产生“机器理解我”的错觉，人机对话的心理效应首次显形。
events.summary_en: In 1965, Joseph Weizenbaum wrote ELIZA in MAD-SLIP on an IBM 7094 at MIT Project MAC, using the CTSS time-sharing system to allow multiple users to converse with the program simultaneously. Designed as a platform that could adopt different personas by swapping "scripts," its most famous was DOCTOR—which mimicked a Rogerian psychotherapist by repackaging user statements into reflective questions like "You said..." and "What does that make you think of?". Published in January 1966 in *CACM* 9(1):36-45, ELIZA instantly became the first program in history that ordinary users treated as genuinely understanding human language.
events.card_summary_en: Simple rules echoing users' own words made people feel understood, and the ELIZA effect was born.
events.why_it_matters_en: ELIZA relied on nothing but simple rules restating users' words, yet created the illusion that the machine understands me, the first surfacing of the psychology of human-machine conversation. It was the first broad experience of a machine seeming to understand you: Weizenbaum's secretary asked him to leave the room after twenty minutes, unwilling to bare her heart to the machine in front of him. The ELIZA effect of users over-identifying with machines remains central to chatbot design and the origin of concerns about anthropomorphic misdirection in evaluating GPT, Claude, and Gemini.
events.behind_scenes_en: Weizenbaum's intent was a platform for studying human-machine conversation, not a chatbot; the DOCTOR script was a casual demonstration that ended up stealing the show, running off, as he put it, to prove things he never intended to prove. Once the magic was discovered, Bernie Cosell rewrote a version in Lisp at BBN and it spread through ARPANET across academia, binding ELIZA to Lisp while the original MAD-SLIP version was forgotten for fifty years. Weizenbaum later wrote Computer Power and Human Reason in 1976 warning against misuse of AI, becoming one of the earliest critics of AI ethics.

events.title_zh: Zadeh 模糊集合:让数学承认“差不多”
events.title_en: Fuzzy Sets
events.summary_zh:
1965 年 6 月,Lotfi Zadeh 在《Information and Control》8(3):338-353 发表《Fuzzy Sets》。
文章定义了“模糊集合”——元素对集合的隶属度不再是 0 或 1,而是 0 到 1 之间的任意实数。
并给出并、交、补等基本运算。
Zadeh 的论点很直接:现实世界中“高”“年轻”“差不多热”这类概念本身就有渐变,经典集合论逼着机器用 0/1 二选一,反而丢掉了人类推理里最关键的灰度信息。
events.source_name: Zadeh, L. A. (1965). Information and Control 8(3):338-353
events.card_summary_zh: 模糊集合允许隶属度处在 0 与 1 之间，让机器第一次能够用数学方式处理“有点像”和“差不多”。
events.summary_en: In June 1965, Lotfi Zadeh published "Fuzzy Sets" in *Information and Control* 8(3):338-353, defining "fuzzy sets"—where an element's membership in a set is no longer a binary 0 or 1, but any real number between 0 and 1—and detailing basic operations like union, intersection, and complement. Zadeh’s argument was straightforward: real-world concepts like "tall," "young," and "about hot" are inherently gradual, and forcing machines to make a binary choice between 0 and 1 via classical set theory discards the crucial gray areas of human reasoning.
events.card_summary_en: Membership between 0 and 1 let mathematics finally handle kind-of and almost.
events.why_it_matters_en: Fuzzy sets let mathematics admit that vagueness itself can be handled precisely. They spawned fuzzy logic and fuzzy control, and in the 1980s-90s Japanese appliances, from Panasonic washers to Mitsubishi air conditioners and the Sendai subway, shipped products that could judge. Washing machines weighing loads, air conditioners holding temperature, and camera autofocus still run fuzzy controllers today. In the LLM era fuzzy sets return as soft labels, membership scores, and token probabilities.
events.behind_scenes_en: Zadeh was born in Azerbaijan to an Iranian family, moved to the United States in 1944, and taught for decades at UC Berkeley. When he wrote Fuzzy Sets he was already an IEEE Fellow and a control-theory authority, yet chose to challenge the roots of classical set theory, drawing nearly twenty years of cold shoulder from the Western mathematical mainstream. Japan and the Soviet Union adopted fastest: the Sendai subway has run on fuzzy control since 1987 with zero accidents, while America only followed at scale in the 1990s. Zadeh lived to 96, dying in 2017, and watched his ideas come back around in the LLM era.

events.title_zh: Amari 用随机梯度下降训练多层感知机
events.title_en: Amari's SGD for Multilayer Perceptrons
events.summary_zh:
1967 年,甘利俊一(Shun-ichi Amari)在日本发表用随机梯度下降(SGD)训练多层感知机的方法,并在 5 层网络(其中 2 层可修改)上做非线性可分模式分类实验。
这是已知最早的端到端梯度训练多层网络的工作——比 Western 文献中广为引用的 Werbos 1974 反向传播早 7 年,比 Rumelhart-Hinton-Williams 1986 的反向传播普及早近 20 年。
events.source_name: Amari, S. (1967). A theory of adaptive pattern classifiers. IEEE Trans. EC-16(3):299-307.
events.card_summary_zh: Amari 用随机梯度下降训练多层感知机；Amari 的工作证明“梯度下降可以训练多层网络”这件事在 1967 年就被解决过一次。
events.summary_en: In 1967, Shun-ichi Amari published a method in Japan for training multilayer perceptrons using stochastic gradient descent (SGD), conducting non-linearly separable pattern classification experiments on a 5-layer network (where 2 layers were modifiable). This is the earliest known work on end-to-end gradient training of multilayer networks—predating the widely cited Werbos 1974 backpropagation in Western literature by 7 years, and the popularization of backpropagation by Rumelhart-Hinton-Williams in 1986 by nearly 20 years.
events.card_summary_en: Amari trained multilayer perceptrons with stochastic gradient descent, solving it once in 1967.
events.why_it_matters_en: His work proved gradient descent can train multilayer networks, settled once back in 1967. That the Minsky-Papert pessimism misled the field for fifteen years owes partly to Amari publishing in Japanese with limited circulation. Today's core training recipe, SGD plus backpropagation, is effectively the synthesis of Amari 1967, Linnainmaa 1970, and Rumelhart 1986.
events.behind_scenes_en: Amari holds a mathematics doctorate from the University of Tokyo and later founded information geometry as a new discipline. His 1967 paper ran in a Japanese domestic journal, so AI history in the English-speaking world long overlooked it. Schmidhuber wrote repeatedly from 2014 to 2024 pressing priority claims for Amari and Ivakhnenko, noting that the Hopfield 1982 network essentially replicates Amari's 1972 adaptive Ising model. Amari received the Kyoto Prize in 2025, after the 2024 physics Nobel for Hopfield and Hinton sparked debate over forgotten Japanese pioneers.

events.title_zh: Winograd SHRDLU:积木世界里的“理解”
events.title_en: SHRDLU: Understanding Natural Language in a Blocks World
events.summary_zh:
1968-1970 年,Terry Winograd 在 MIT 开发 SHRDLU,作为博士论文(1970 完成;论文 1971 年以 MIT AI-TR-235 正式发表)。
程序运行在 DEC PDP-6 上,用 Micro Planner + Lisp 写成,用户通过电传打字机与一个虚拟“积木世界”对话——指令 SHRDLU 把红色方块放到绿色立方体上,问“刚才你拿起的是哪个?”,SHRDLU 会回答、追问、纠正、推理。
1972 年论文以《Understanding Natural Language》出书(Academic Press),被认为是 1970 年代自然语言理解的最高成就。
events.source_name: Winograd, T. (1972). Understanding Natural Language. Academic Press. PhD thesis, MIT, 1970.
events.card_summary_zh: SHRDLU 能听懂指令、追踪上下文并操作虚拟积木，却也暴露了 AI 一离开封闭世界就会失灵的边界。
events.summary_en: Between 1968 and 1970, Terry Winograd developed SHRDLU at MIT for his PhD thesis, which was completed in 1970 and officially published in 1971 as MIT AI-TR-235. Running on a DEC PDP-6 and written in Micro Planner and Lisp, the program allowed users to converse with a virtual "blocks world" via teletype—instructing SHRDLU to put a red block on a green cube or asking "which one did you just pick up?" as the system answered, asked follow-up questions, corrected, and reasoned. In 1972, the thesis was published as a book, *Understanding Natural Language* (Academic Press), and went on to be recognized as the crowning achievement of 1970s natural language understanding.
events.card_summary_en: SHRDLU took instructions, tracked context, and moved blocks, exposing AI's closed-world limits.
events.why_it_matters_en: For the first time a program looked like it genuinely understood language, combining syntax, semantics, reasoning, memory, and planning into a visible engineering system. Later NLP researchers either patched SHRDLU's path or, like Winograd himself, turned against it: by the late 1970s at Stanford he shifted to HCI and Heidegger, arguing the route fails because it depends on a closed world, a reflection that steered NLP through the 1980s-90s.
events.behind_scenes_en: Winograd was then 24, supervised by Marvin Minsky. The name comes from ETAOIN SHRDLU, the second row of Linotype keys ordered by letter frequency, the garbled placeholder of old typesetting errors. SHRDLU looked like a general dialogue system but worked only inside a fifty-word blocks world, the peak and endpoint of the 1960s microworld route. Winograd later reflected that we assumed enlarging the blocks world gave the real one, but the real world has no clean boundaries and no perfectly aligned semantics, a line quoted again and again in the LLM era: is GPT-4 just a bigger SHRDLU that seems to understand?

events.title_zh: Knuth《The Art of Computer Programming》Vol.1 出版
events.title_en: Knuth: The Art of Computer Programming, Vol. 1 (1968)
events.summary_zh:
1968 年,Donald Knuth 出版《The Art of Computer Programming》第一卷《Fundamental Algorithms》。
Knuth 计划写 7 卷,到 2024 年只出了 1-4A 卷,但已完成的卷被誉为“算法圣经”,是计算机科学作为独立学科的奠基文献之一。
Knuth 同时启动 TeX 排版项目(1977),其结果 TeX/LaTeX 成为之后 50 年所有科学论文的标准排版工具。
events.source_name: Knuth, D. E. (1968). The Art of Computer Programming, Vol. 1. Addison-Wesley.
events.card_summary_zh: Knuth《The Art of Computer Programming》Vol.1 出版。
events.summary_en: In 1968, Donald Knuth published *Fundamental Algorithms*, the first volume of *The Art of Computer Programming*. Although Knuth planned for seven volumes, only Volumes 1-4A have been released as of 2024, yet the completed work is hailed as the "bible of algorithms" and stands as a founding text of computer science as an independent discipline. Knuth also launched the TeX typesetting project (1977), resulting in TeX/LaTeX, which became the standard typesetting tool for all scientific papers over the next 50 years.
events.card_summary_en: TAOCP lifted algorithms from engineering practice into provable, analyzable mathematical objects.
events.why_it_matters_en: It raised algorithms into mathematical objects you can prove things about, the methodological source of all algorithm-complexity analysis, model-efficiency work, and FLOPS accounting in the AI era. Knuth's literate programming idea lives on in the code-plus-narrative style of Jupyter notebooks and Observable, and premature optimization is the root of all evil remains engineering's most quoted maxim.
events.behind_scenes_en: In 1962, still a Caltech graduate student, Knuth was approached by an Addison-Wesley editor to write a small compiler book. It kept growing; volume one passed 600 pages by publication in 1968. Knuth himself estimated completion needed another twenty years, and sixty years on it remains unfinished. He long ran Computer Musings lectures at Stanford, saying publicly in 2014 that he had given up finishing all seven volumes in his lifetime but would bring each to a state worth finishing. He stayed close to AI academia, his doctoral students including Vaughan Pratt, though Robert Tarjan's formal advisor was Robert Floyd with Knuth only one of his academic advisors.

events.title_zh: Engelbart「演示之母」:NLS 与个人计算诞生
events.title_en: The Mother of All Demos (Engelbart, 1968-12-09)
events.summary_zh:
1968 年 12 月 9 日,Douglas Engelbart 在旧金山 Fall Joint Computer Conference 上做了 90 分钟演示,首次公开展示 NLS(oN-Line System):鼠标、超文本链接、实时文字编辑、屏幕窗口、视频会议、协作文档、版本控制——今天个人计算的所有核心要素。
Engelbart 远程连线 SRI 实验室,让团队现场协作编辑一份结构化文档。
演示被称作“The Mother of All Demos”——之后的 Apple Macintosh 发布(1984)、iPhone 发布(2007)都被视作它的延续。
events.source_name: Engelbart, D. (1968). A Research Center for Augmenting Human Intellect. FJCC.
events.card_summary_zh: Engelbart「演示之母」：NLS 与个人计算诞生；次演示定义了“人机交互”作为独立学科的边界。
events.summary_en: On December 9, 1968, Douglas Engelbart delivered a 90-minute presentation at the Fall Joint Computer Conference in San Francisco, publicly debuting NLS (oN-Line System) to showcase the mouse, hypertext links, real-time text editing, screen windows, video conferencing, collaborative documents, and version control—all the core elements of modern personal computing. Connecting remotely to the SRI lab to collaboratively edit a structured document live with his team, Engelbart pulled off what became legendary as "The Mother of All Demos," a landmark event whose lineage continues through the subsequent launches of the Apple Macintosh (1984) and the iPhone (2007).
events.card_summary_en: Engelbart's 1968 demo drew the boundary lines of human-computer interaction as its own field.
events.why_it_matters_en: That single demo fixed HCI as an independent discipline. Mouse, hyperlinks, and collaborative editing were commercialized by Apple, Microsoft, and Tim Berners-Lee in the 1980s-90s and became the basis of every desktop and mobile device today. Engelbart's augmentation route, IA, is mainstream again in the LLM era: Notion AI, Cursor, and Copilot all extend his 1968 vision.
events.behind_scenes_en: Reading Vannevar Bush's As We May Think in the 1950s, Engelbart resolved to build memex. In 1962 he published Augmenting Human Intellect: A Conceptual Framework and won ARPA funding for SRI's Augmentation Research Center. The 1968 demo connected back to SRI over dedicated links, microwave video plus audio return, and an audience above a thousand watched a link clicked with a mouse without grasping they were seeing the embryo of the next fifty years of computing. Engelbart felt lifelong that Silicon Valley took his ideas without credit; even Apple's 1979 PARC visit to study the Alto drew on NLS thinking.

events.title_zh: Minsky-Papert《Perceptrons》:神经网络第一次大挫折
events.title_en: Perceptrons (Minsky & Papert, MIT Press, 1969)
events.summary_zh:
1969 年,Marvin Minsky 和 Seymour Papert 出版《Perceptrons: An Introduction to Computational Geometry》(MIT Press)。
书中用严格数学证明:单层感知机无法表达 XOR、连通性等基本函数,要表达这些函数必须靠多层网络,而多层网络当时没有可用的训练算法。
1988 年扩展版(含 Epilogue)承认原版部分论断被过度外推——但 1969 年原版引发的“神经网络死路”印象已经形成,直接促成 1970 年代第一次 AI 寒冬。
events.source_name: Minsky, M. & Papert, S. (1969). Perceptrons. MIT Press.
events.card_summary_zh: Minsky-Papert《Perceptrons》：神经网络第一次大挫折；是 AI 史上被引用最多、误读最多的一本书。
events.summary_en: In 1969, Marvin Minsky and Seymour Papert published *Perceptrons: An Introduction to Computational Geometry* (MIT Press), proving mathematically that single-layer perceptrons could not represent basic functions like XOR or connectivity, which required multi-layer networks that lacked viable training algorithms at the time. While their 1988 expanded edition (including an Epilogue) admitted that some of these claims had been over-extrapolated, the original book had already cemented the impression that neural networks were a dead end, directly triggering the first AI winter of the 1970s.
events.card_summary_en: AI's most cited and most misread book brought neural networks their first great setback.
events.why_it_matters_en: The book discussed only single-layer perceptrons but was read as all neural networks fail, drying up research money through the 1970s-80s and driving researchers out of the field. When Rosenblatt died in a 1971 boating accident, nobody carried on his multilayer work. Only the 1986 Rumelhart-Hinton-Williams backpropagation paper broke the misreading, and on winning the Nobel in 2024 Hinton still spoke of this book's hold on him.
events.behind_scenes_en: While Minsky and Papert wrote it, Rosenblatt was their colleague and friend. The text never declares neural networks dead, but the last chapter of the 1969 first edition leaned hard on constructions like the perceptron will not, and MIT Press marketing cemented the public sense that AI academia had pronounced them finished. Papert later admitted they meant to write a rigorous book and produced a bomb instead. Rosenblatt never got to defend himself, lost in a boating accident on his 43rd birthday in July 1971, and American neural-network funding reportedly fell some ninety percent in the five years after his death, ratio pending verification.

events.title_zh: SRI Shakey:第一个会推理的移动机器人
events.title_en: Shakey: First Mobile Robot with Reasoning
events.summary_zh:
1966-1972 年,SRI International(Charles Rosen + Nils Nilsson 团队)开发 Shakey——第一个能感知环境、规划路径、执行动作的自主移动机器人。
1969 年第一版完成:装电视摄像头、激光测距仪、碰撞传感器,通过无线连到 DEC PDP-10/PDP-15 上跑规划与感知。
1971-1972 年 Fikes+Nilsson 发表 STRIPS 规划器,把“动作 = 前提条件 + 删除表 + 添加表”形式化,成为之后 30 年机器人规划的事实标准。
events.source_name: Nilsson, N. J. (1984). Shakey the Robot. SRI AI Center Technical Note 323.
events.card_summary_zh: Shakey 把感知、规划和行动装进同一台移动机器人，第一次让机器根据环境自主决定下一步。
events.summary_en: From 1966 to 1972, SRI International (led by Charles Rosen and Nils Nilsson) developed Shakey, the first autonomous mobile robot capable of perceiving its environment, planning paths, and executing actions. Completed in 1969, the first version carried a TV camera, a laser rangefinder, and bump sensors, wirelessly connecting to a DEC PDP-10/PDP-15 to run its planning and perception. In 1971-1972, Fikes and Nilsson published the STRIPS planner, formalizing "action = preconditions + delete list + add list" into the de facto standard for robot planning for the next 30 years.
events.card_summary_en: Shakey packed perception, planning, and action into one mobile robot choosing its own next move.
events.why_it_matters_en: Shakey contributed A* search, the Hough transform, visibility graphs, STRIPS, and layered architecture at once, the algorithmic bedrock of every mobile robot since, from vacuum cleaners and self-driving cars to Mars rovers and warehouse robots. Inducted into Carnegie Mellon's Robot Hall of Fame in 2004, its line lives on in OpenAI-era robot research and Waymo path planning through STRIPS variants.
events.behind_scenes_en: The name came from its wobbly gait, the rooftop camera so heavy the robot often paused mid-move. Charles Rosen proposed the project in 1963, the proposal went to DARPA in 1965 securing 750,000 dollars, about 5.8 million today, figure pending verification, and launch followed in 1966. At the first complete demonstration in 1969 Shakey independently found an object in a room and pushed it aside, and Life magazine called it the first electronic person. Nilsson later recalled expecting household robots within ten years, a road still unfinished after fifty.

events.title_zh: Minsky 获 ACM Turing Award:AI 第一次拿“计算机诺贝尔”
events.title_en: Marvin Minsky Receives ACM Turing Award
events.summary_zh:
1969 年,ACM 将图灵奖颁给 Marvin Minsky,表彰他在《Computation: Finite and Infinite Machines》(1967)、《Semantic Information Processing》(1968) 等著作中对计算理论、AI、认知科学的综合贡献。
Minsky 是 AI 领域第一位图灵奖得主,比 Dijkstra(1972)、McCarthy(1971)、Newell-Simon(1975)都早。
events.source_name: ACM Turing Award citation, Marvin Minsky, 1969
events.card_summary_zh: Minsky 成为首位获得图灵奖的 AI 研究者，人工智能由此正式进入计算机科学最高荣誉的核心视野。
events.summary_en: In 1969, the ACM awarded the Turing Award to Marvin Minsky, recognizing his comprehensive contributions to computation theory, AI, and cognitive science in works such as *Computation: Finite and Infinite Machines* (1967) and *Semantic Information Processing* (1968). Minsky was the first Turing Award winner in the field of AI, preceding Dijkstra (1972), McCarthy (1971), and Newell-Simon (1975).
events.card_summary_en: Minsky became the first AI researcher to take the Turing Award, AI entering computing's honors.
events.why_it_matters_en: The award itself marked AI's formal recognition by mainstream computer science at the end of the 1960s. McCarthy in 1971, Newell and Simon in 1975, Feigenbaum in 1994, Pearl in 2011, and Hinton, LeCun, and Bengio in 2018 followed, steadily consolidating the discipline's standing. Minsky's Turing lecture Form and Content in Computer Science became a classic, insisting programs must be comprehensible to people and not merely correct.
events.behind_scenes_en: Born in New York in 1927, Minsky took his mathematics doctorate at Princeton and built SNARC in 1951, the first neural-network learning machine, with 40 neurons and adjustable weights. He joined MIT in 1958 and co-founded the AI Project with McCarthy. Practically single-handed he trained a roster of leading scholars, Terry Winograd, Patrick Winston, Gerald Sussman, and collaborator Seymour Papert, who carried AI through the 1970s-80s. He died in 2016, only two years before Hinton and company took the 2018 award, missing the LLM-era eruption built on foundations he laid in 1969.

events.title_zh: IJCAI-1 第一届国际人工智能联合会议
events.title_en: First International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI-1)
events.summary_zh:
1969 年 5 月 7-9 日,第一届 IJCAI 在华盛顿举行,由 Allen Newell、Marvin Minsky、John McCarthy、Arthur Samuel 等发起,60 多位研究者参加。
会议确立了 AI 作为独立学科的学术共同体身份,首次把分散在 IEEE、ACM、心理学、控制论等领域的 AI 研究者聚到一起。
之后 IJCAI 变成两年一次的旗舰会议,1979 年 AAAI 成立后与之并行。
events.source_name: IJCAI-1 Proceedings (1969). Washington, D.C., May 7-9.
events.card_summary_zh: 首届 IJCAI 把分散在计算机、心理学与控制论中的研究者聚到一起，AI 从研究方向成长为国际学术共同体。
events.summary_en: From May 7–9, 1969, the inaugural IJCAI was held in Washington, initiated by Allen Newell, Marvin Minsky, John McCarthy, Arthur Samuel, and others, with over 60 researchers in attendance. The event established AI’s identity as an independent academic discipline, bringing together researchers previously scattered across IEEE, ACM, psychology, cybernetics, and other fields. IJCAI subsequently became a biennial flagship conference, running in parallel with AAAI after its founding in 1979.
events.card_summary_en: The first IJCAI united researchers across computing, psychology, and cybernetics as one community.
events.why_it_matters_en: IJCAI is where AI's institutional life began. Before it, AI papers scattered across whatever conference would take them; after it, AI had a home field. When the 1973 Lighthill Report slashed British funding, the IJCAI community was among the few forces able to answer collectively. NeurIPS, ICML, and ICLR today all trace their model back to IJCAI-1.
events.behind_scenes_en: The proceedings ran only 643 pages, page count pending verification, with some sixty attendees, against IJCAI 2023's 5,000-plus papers and 10,000-plus participants, a measure of how small the circle still was in 1969. Main topics were theorem proving, vision, planning, natural language, and knowledge representation, still AI's core agenda sixty years later with Lisp swapped for PyTorch. Marvin Minsky's opening address predicted AI would settle most intellectual problems within twenty years, an optimism that became an ironic footnote of the coming winters.

events.title_zh: Linnainmaa 反向模式自动微分
events.title_en: Linnainmaa's Reverse-Mode Automatic Differentiation
events.summary_zh:
1970 年,芬兰数学家 Seppo Linnainmaa 在赫尔辛基大学硕士论文《The representation of the cumulative rounding error of an algorithm as a Taylor expansion of the local rounding errors》中首次给出反向模式自动微分的完整算法描述,把链式法则从输出端往输入端递归展开,把任意复合函数的偏导数压缩到一次正向 + 一次反向扫描。
这就是后来深度学习训练里“反向传播”的数学本体。
论文本身用 Fortran 做浮点舍入误差分析,只字未提神经网络。
events.source_name: Linnainmaa, S. (1970). M.Sc. thesis, University of Helsinki; (1976) BIT 16(2):146-160
events.card_summary_zh: Linnainmaa 反向模式自动微分；反向模式 AD 是整个深度学习的底层齿轮。
events.summary_en: In 1970, Finnish mathematician Seppo Linnainmaa first described the complete algorithm for reverse-mode automatic differentiation in his University of Helsinki master’s thesis, *The representation of the cumulative rounding error of an algorithm as a Taylor expansion of the local rounding errors*, recursively expanding the chain rule from output to input to compress the partial derivatives of any composite function into a single forward and backward pass. This became the mathematical essence of "backpropagation" in deep learning training. Yet, the thesis itself used Fortran to analyze floating-point rounding errors and never once mentioned neural networks.
events.card_summary_en: Reverse-mode automatic differentiation is the low-level gear underneath all of deep learning.
events.why_it_matters_en: Every training run behind GPT, Stable Diffusion, and AlphaFold rests on this scan: evaluate forward once, then compute every partial derivative backward in a single pass. Grasping the 1970 line makes clear how mathematics often arrives decades before machines and compute catch up.
events.behind_scenes_en: Linnainmaa wrote the paper as neural networks touched bottom. Minsky and Papert's Perceptrons had just come out in 1969 and connectionism was broadly written off. Working in that climate, he framed reverse-mode AD purely as a numerical computing tool, unaware it unlocked precisely the deadlock of untrainable multilayer perceptrons. Schmidhuber and others excavated the paper twenty-four years later, and the field discovered backpropagation's mathematics had been lying in Finland for over two decades.

events.title_zh: SHRDLU:最早的自然语言理解程序
events.title_en: SHRDLU: Natural Language Understanding in a Blocks World
events.summary_zh:
1968-1970 年,Terry Winograd 在 MIT 完成博士论文《Procedures as a Representation for Datain a Computer Program for Understanding Natural Language》,1970 年初答辩,1971 年作为 MIT AI TR-235 正式发表。
SHRDLU 让用户用普通英语指挥一个虚拟“积木世界”里的机械臂:“把那个红色方块放到蓝色立方体上”,“刚才你碰过那个金字塔吗”。
程序能理解指代、时态、上下文、规划与回指,并能解释自己的操作理由。
在 1970 年的算力下,它在封闭世界里达成了惊人的语言理解水平。
events.source_name: Winograd, T. (1971). MIT AI TR-235; (1972) Cognitive Psychology 3(1):1-191
events.card_summary_zh: SHRDLU 能在积木世界中理解指令与上下文，既代表符号语言理解的高峰，也暴露了封闭环境的局限。
events.summary_en: Between 1968 and 1970, Terry Winograd wrote his MIT doctoral thesis, "Procedures as a Representation for Data in a Computer Program for Understanding Natural Language"—defending it in early 1970 and officially publishing it in 1971 as MIT AI TR-235. His program, SHRDLU, allowed users to command a robotic arm in a virtual "blocks world" using plain English, such as "put that red block on the blue cube" or "did you touch that pyramid just now?" Despite the limited computing power of 1970, it achieved an astonishing level of language understanding within a closed world, handling reference, tense, context, planning, and anaphora, while even explaining the logic behind its actions.
events.card_summary_en: Inside its tiny blocks world SHRDLU tracked instructions and context, symbolic NLP's peak.
events.why_it_matters_en: SHRDLU is both the summit of symbolic NLP and the start of its decline. It proved a small world plus strong rules can carry language understanding, and exposed the deadlock that rules explode once the world grows. Today's LLMs attack Winograd's problem by another road, statistics plus massive data, yet the blocks-world paradigm remains a standard model for teaching and testing reasoning.
events.behind_scenes_en: Its success rested on three hidden limits: a world of a few dozen blocks with a short vocabulary; grammar rules and semantic networks hand-written line by line by Winograd; and a PDP-6 or PDP-10 running a LISP interpreter on very small memory. Reviewing the work in Cognitive Science in 1980, Winograd said he had underestimated how hard it would be to extend any of it to the real world. The better SHRDLU performed, the more people believed natural language would fall to writing enough rules.

events.title_zh: Intel 4004:首颗商用微处理器
events.title_en: Intel 4004: First Commercial Microprocessor
events.summary_zh:
1971 年 11 月 15 日,Intel 发布 4004 微处理器。
这是全球第一款商用单芯片微处理器,把一台完整中央处理器的逻辑(2300 个晶体管,740 kHz,4 位字长,10 微米工艺)压进 16 针 DIP 封装里。
Federico Faggin、Marcian Hoff、Stanley Mazor 设计,Busicom 计算器是原始客户。
Intel 以 6 万美元从 Busicom 买回 4004 的非独家授权,允许 Intel 把它当通用产品卖。
这是微处理器从“为某个客户定制”变成“通用计算元件”的转折点。
events.source_name: Intel 4004 datasheet (1971); Faggin, F. (2009) IEEE Annals of the History of Computing 31(2)
events.card_summary_zh: Intel 发布 4004 微处理器；微处理器让算力从机房走进桌面、家庭和工厂。
events.summary_en: On November 15, 1971, Intel released the 4004, the world's first commercial single-chip microprocessor, which packed the logic of a complete CPU (2300 transistors, 740 kHz, 4-bit word length, 10-micron process) into a 16-pin DIP package. Designed by Federico Faggin, Marcian Hoff, and Stanley Mazor with the Busicom calculator as the original customer, the project became the turning point where microprocessors transitioned from custom-made client chips to universal computing components after Intel bought back the non-exclusive rights from Busicom for $60,000 to sell it as a general-purpose product.
events.card_summary_en: The 4004 carried computing power out of the machine room toward desks, homes, and factories.
events.why_it_matters_en: Microprocessors made compute cheap and widespread. Without this hardware line there is no Altair in 1975, no Apple II in 1977, no IBM PC in 1981, and none of the soil that later let individuals train neural networks in their bedrooms.
events.behind_scenes_en: Before the 4004, a computer's CPU was a whole cabinet of circuit boards no small company could afford. At sixty dollars a chip, the 4004 turned computing into a retailable component. Faggin later left Intel to found Zilog and built the Z80, igniting the eight-bit personal computer era. For AI the significance was never raw speed but the premise that computing could be packaged, sold, and fitted into anything; PCs, embedded systems, robots, GPUs, and TPUs all rest on retailable compute elements.

events.title_zh: Prolog:逻辑编程语言问世
events.title_en: Prolog: First Logic Programming Language
events.summary_zh:
1972 年,Alain Colmerauer 和 Philippe Roussel 在马赛大学(Luminy)设计出 Prolog(Programmation en Logique)。
Robert Kowalski 同期在爱丁堡给出 SLD 反驳消解的理论基础,即“算法 = 逻辑 + 控制”。
Prolog 把程序员的角色改成两件事:写事实,写规则,机器自己用反演推理找答案。
1977 年 Warren 在爱丁堡实现首个 Prolog 编译器(DEC-10 Prolog);1983 年又设计了 Warren 抽象机(WAM),成为日后 Prolog 编译的事实标准,在 1980 年代成为欧洲 AI 和日本第五代计算机计划的核心语言。
events.source_name: Colmerauer, A. & Roussel, P. (1972); Kowalski, R. (1974) IFIP Congress
events.card_summary_zh: Prolog：逻辑编程语言问世；Prolog 让“声明式编程”和“逻辑推理引擎”进入主流。
events.summary_en: In 1972, Alain Colmerauer and Philippe Roussel designed Prolog (Programmation en Logique) at the University of Marseille (Luminy), while Robert Kowalski in Edinburgh established the theoretical foundation of SLD resolution refutation, "Algorithm = Logic + Control." The language shifted the programmer’s job to simply writing facts and rules, leaving the machine to find answers through deductive reasoning. In 1977, Warren implemented the first Prolog compiler (DEC-10 Prolog) in Edinburgh, later designing the Warren Abstract Machine (WAM) in 1983, which became the de facto compilation standard and the core language of European AI and Japan’s Fifth Generation Computer Systems project in the 1980s.
events.card_summary_en: Prolog brought declarative programming and logic inference engines into the mainstream.
events.why_it_matters_en: It shaped a generation of knowledge representation, expert systems, constraint solving, and natural-language interface design. Though no longer mainstream, Prolog's shadow persists in Datalog, SQL three-valued logic, rule engines, and graph-database query languages.
events.behind_scenes_en: Two streams converged into Prolog. Colmerauer was building a natural-language question-answerer and needed a tool handling yes, no, and list answers; Kowalski worked on automated theorem proving and Horn clause resolution. The two met through Marseille meetings in 1971 and 1972 and merged their lines. In 1982 Japan's Fifth Generation Computer project picked Prolog as its base language, making it the AI world's second language alongside LISP through the early 1980s.

events.title_zh: Lighthill 报告:英国 AI 第一次大裁员
events.title_en: Lighthill Report: AI General Survey
events.summary_zh:
1973 年,英国科学研究委员会(SRC)出版《Artificial Intelligence: a paper symposium》,卷首是 Sir James Lighthill 撰写的《Artificial Intelligence: A General Survey》。
Lighthill 把 AI 分成 A(高级自动化)、B(机器人等搭桥研究)、C(中枢神经系统的计算机模拟)。
他直接批评 A 类(定理证明)和 B 类(机器人)研究在“组合爆炸”面前束手无策,结论是“在所有领域,已取得的发现都没有产生当时承诺的重大影响”。
报告导致英国政府除爱丁堡、苏塞克斯、埃塞克斯三校外,停止对其他大学的 AI 研究资助,直接引发英国第一次 AI 寒冬。
events.source_name: Lighthill, J. (1973). Artificial Intelligence: A General Survey. SRC Paper Symposium
events.card_summary_zh: Lighthill 报告：英国 AI 第一次大裁员；Lighthill 报告是 AI 史上第一次“外部审计”触发寒冬的样本。
events.summary_en: In 1973, the British Science Research Council (SRC) published *Artificial Intelligence: a paper symposium*, opening with Sir James Lighthill’s *Artificial Intelligence: A General Survey*. Lighthill divided AI into Category A (advanced automation), Category B (bridge research like robotics), and Category C (computer simulation of the central nervous system), directly criticizing Category A (theorem proving) and Category B (robotics) as helpless against "combinatorial explosion." Concluding that "in no part of the field have the discoveries made so far produced the major impact that was then promised," the report led the British government to halt AI research funding for all universities except Edinburgh, Sussex, and Essex, directly triggering the UK's first AI winter.
events.card_summary_en: The Lighthill Report is AI history's first case of an outside audit triggering a winter.
events.why_it_matters_en: It showed AI is never only a technical matter; expectation management, funding structure, institutional politics, and press sentiment all decide survival. The winter talk and generative-AI bubble debates of 2023-2025 replay the same law: when promises go unredeemed, external review and policy tightening arrive together.
events.behind_scenes_en: The fuse had two layers. Technically, touring Edinburgh's machine intelligence department, Lighthill watched many demonstration systems collapse outside their little worlds and judged the gap between promise and reality too wide. Politically, Michie's long-running conflict with the sitting department head produced complaint letters to SRC, which wanted an external review to sort out where AI money went. The two forces together turned an internal assessment into the budget axe over British AI. Lighthill himself was no opponent of AI and later conceded parts of the report were too harsh.

events.title_zh: AARON:最早的长周期 AI 艺术系统
events.title_en: AARON: Early Long-Running AI Art System
events.summary_zh:
1973 年前后,英国艺术家 Harold Cohen 在加州大学圣地亚哥分校(UCSD)开始编写 AARON 绘画程序。
AARON 不是一次性生成器,而是 Cohen 用了 40 多年不断迭代的“合作者”。
早期版本(1970s)用规则在屏幕上画闭合轮廓与色块;1980 年代扩展到毛笔、岩石、植物造型;1990 年代加入色彩决策,程序能自己选颜色。
Cohen 后期让 AARON 直接驱动画布机械臂,真画物理水彩和丙烯。
events.source_name: Cohen, H. (1973-2010); Computer History Museum retrospective
events.card_summary_zh: AARON：最早的长周期 AI 艺术系统；AARON 把 AI 艺术史拉长到半个世纪。
events.summary_en: Around 1973, British artist Harold Cohen began writing the AARON painting program at the University of California, San Diego (UCSD), creating a "collaborator" he would iteratively develop for over 40 years rather than a simple one-off generator. While 1970s versions used rules to draw closed outlines and color blocks on screens, AARON expanded to brush, rock, and plant forms in the 1980s, and gained color decision-making in the 1990s to choose its own palette. Later on, Cohen had the program directly drive robotic arms to paint physical watercolors and acrylics onto canvas.
events.card_summary_en: AARON stretches AI art history across half a century.
events.why_it_matters_en: Anyone debating today whether AI can be an artist finds in AARON that the tangle of tools, rules, randomness, and authorship is a long-running question of AI art, not something newly invented in 2022.
events.behind_scenes_en: Discussion of AI art defaults to DALL-E or diffusion models, but AARON pushes the line back fifty years. Cohen's core question was never whether a machine can draw but how authorship divides. He consistently refused to call AARON an independent artist, insisting on final attribution rights himself, a question that returned as a legal and ethical focus in the generative AI era.

events.title_zh: WABOT-1:第一台全尺寸人形机器人
events.title_en: WABOT-1: First Full-Scale Humanoid Robot
events.summary_zh:
1973 年,早稻田大学加藤一郎实验室完成 WABOT-1(WAseda roBOT 1)。
它身高 1.6 米,重 130 公斤,由四个子系统组成:WAMOT-1(机械臂,5 自由度 + 抓持)、WL-5(下肢,液压驱动,静步态行走)、视觉系统(接触 / 触觉 / 简易距离感)、语音系统(简单元音识别和合成)。
走一步大约 45 秒,但能自主完成“看 - 走 - 抓 - 简单对话”闭环。
events.source_name: Kato, I. (1973). Waseda Univ. Bioengineering Lab report; humanoid.waseda.ac.jp
events.card_summary_zh: 早稻田大学加藤一郎实验室完成 WABOT-1(WAseda roBOT 1)；WABOT-1 是具身智能史的第一座里程碑。
events.summary_en: In 1973, Ichiro Kato’s laboratory at Waseda University completed WABOT-1 (WAseda roBOT 1). Standing 1.6 meters tall and weighing 130 kilograms, it was composed of four subsystems: WAMOT-1 (a robotic arm with 5 degrees of freedom and gripping), WL-5 (hydraulically driven lower limbs for static gait walking), a vision system (contact, tactile, and simple distance sensing), and a voice system (simple vowel recognition and synthesis). Although it took about 45 seconds to take a single step, it could autonomously complete the closed loop of "seeing, walking, grasping, and simple conversation."
events.card_summary_en: Waseda University's Kato laboratory completed WABOT-1, embodied intelligence's first milestone.
events.why_it_matters_en: WABOT-1 moved AI out of on-screen conversation into a body in a real room, instantly exposing fresh problems stacked from intelligence plus gravity plus friction plus sensing delay. The technical trees of Honda ASIMO, Boston Dynamics Atlas, and Tesla Optimus all hold early prototypes inside WABOT-1's subsystems.
events.behind_scenes_en: The hard part was not walking but not falling. It used a static gait, shifting its center of gravity over the support foot before lifting the other, with pressure sensors underfoot reporting weight position in real time. Driven by relays and hydraulics it was enormous and power-hungry, and 1973 compute could not attempt real-time dynamic balance, so Kato's team used mechanical engineering and physiology to simplify the problem until a machine could run it.

events.title_zh: Xerox Alto:第一台图形界面个人计算机
events.title_en: Xerox Alto: First GUI Personal Computer
events.summary_zh:
1973 年 3 月 1 日,Xerox PARC 的 Alto 计算机首次运行。
由 Butler Lampson 提案(1972 年 12 月备忘录),Chuck Thacker 主导硬件设计,Robert Metcalfe 与 David Boggs 发明以太网。
Alto 把“位图显示 + 鼠标 + 三键 + 窗口 + WYSIWYG 文档 + 局域网 + 激光打印机”整合到一台机器里。
这是 Steve Jobs 1979 年参观 PARC 看到的“未来”,直接催生 Apple Lisa 和 Macintosh。
events.source_name: Thacker, C. et al. (1979) Xerox Alto; Turing Award 2009
events.card_summary_zh: Xerox PARC 的 Alto 计算机首次运行；Alto 决定了今天所有个人计算设备的视觉和交互范式。
events.summary_en: On March 1, 1973, Xerox PARC’s Alto computer ran for the first time; proposed in a December 1972 memo by Butler Lampson, its hardware design was led by Chuck Thacker, while Robert Metcalfe and David Boggs invented Ethernet. The Alto integrated a bitmap display, a mouse, three buttons, windows, WYSIWYG documents, a local area network, and a laser printer into a single machine. This was the "future" Steve Jobs saw during his 1979 visit to PARC, directly spawning the Apple Lisa and Macintosh.
events.card_summary_en: Xerox PARC's Alto first ran, fixing the look and interaction of every personal device since.
events.why_it_matters_en: Alto decided the visual and interaction paradigm of personal computing today. For AI, graphics plus mouse moved conversing with machines from command-line specialists to everyone, preparing the user base for MATLAB, Jupyter, and AI toolchains on PCs. Thacker received the 2009 Turing Award for the Alto design.
events.behind_scenes_en: Each Alto cost 12,000 dollars and PARC built roughly 2,000, but Xerox executives never commercialized it, reasoning that personal computers had no market. When Jobs brought the Apple team through PARC in 1979 and saw Smalltalk, Alto, bitmap editing, and overlapping windows, those ideas went home into the Lisa in 1983 and Macintosh in 1984, with Windows 1.0 continuing the Mac line in 1985. PARC invented the GUI; Apple and Microsoft made it a mass product.

events.title_zh: 第一次 AI 寒冬:英美同步降温
events.title_en: First AI Winter Begins
events.summary_zh:
1973-1974 年,英美 AI 经费同步大砍,构成第一次 AI 寒冬。
英国:Lighthill 报告(1973)导致 SRC 停止对爱丁堡之外多数大学的 AI 资助。
美国:DARPA 1969 年 Mansfield 修正案后必须证明项目“直接军事相关”,1971-1974 年大幅削减 CMU、MIT、SRI、斯坦福的 AI 通用研究经费,1974 年的 DARPA AI 研究预算比 1968 年下降约 30%。
学术界:Minsky 与 Papert《Perceptrons》(1969)被误读为“神经网络已死”,连接主义研究在 70 年代几乎断流。
events.source_name: Crevier, G. (1993). AI: The Tumultuous History; McCorduck 2004; Russell & Norvig 3rd ed.
events.card_summary_zh: 承诺远超实际能力后，英美资助机构同时收紧经费，AI 第一次为过度乐观付出整个行业的代价。
events.summary_en: The first AI winter set in during 1973–1974 as the UK and US simultaneously slashed funding: the UK’s Lighthill Report (1973) led the SRC to halt AI funding for most universities except Edinburgh. In the US, the 1969 Mansfield Amendment required projects to be "directly military-related," prompting DARPA to drastically cut general AI research funding at CMU, MIT, SRI, and Stanford between 1971 and 1974, leaving the agency's 1974 AI budget down about 30% compared to 1968. Meanwhile, in academia, Minsky and Papert’s *Perceptrons* (1969) was misread as declaring "neural networks are dead," causing connectionist research to almost completely dry up in the 1970s.
events.card_summary_en: With promises far past capability, British and American funders cut at once, billing all of AI.
events.why_it_matters_en: The first winter is AI history's most complete promise-reality-punishment loop. Understanding it explains why sticking with neural networks in the 1990s made Hinton and LeCun look stubborn beyond reason, and where the dread in post-2023 bubble talk originates. AI's history is never one-way progress but cycles of overheating, winter, and recovery.
events.behind_scenes_en: The winter was three forces stacked. Technical: machine translation, machine vision, and speech recognition missed 1960s promises, and combinatorial explosion stalled general problem solvers on real tasks. Economic: the 1973 oil shock and US recession squeezed government research budgets everywhere. Institutional: DARPA stopped tolerating pure scientific curiosity and demanded deliverable military value. Pressed together, they demoted AI from tomorrow's star to over-promising failure; students stopped enrolling, professors switched fields, and the cold lasted until expert systems revived things in 1980.

events.title_zh: Minsky 框架理论:知识表示的新结构
events.title_en: Minsky Frames: A Framework for Representing Knowledge
events.summary_zh:
1974 年 6 月,Marvin Minsky 在 MIT AI Lab Memo 306 发表《A Framework for Representing Knowledge》,1975 年收录进 Winston 编辑的《The Psychology of Computer Vision》。
论文提出“框架(Frame)”数据结构:一个框架描述一类刻板场景(如“走进客厅”),顶部是固定信息,底部是若干“槽(slot)”装具体实例,槽有默认值,可被子框架覆盖。
框架之间组成“框架系统”,通过变换表示视角、动作和因果关系。
events.source_name: Minsky, M. (1974). MIT-AI Memo 306; (1975) in Winston (ed.) Psychology of Computer Vision
events.card_summary_zh: 框架理论用槽位和默认值组织场景知识，为机器表示人物、物体、动作和因果关系提供了新结构。
events.summary_en: In June 1974, Marvin Minsky published "A Framework for Representing Knowledge" as MIT AI Lab Memo 306, which was later included in the 1975 book *The Psychology of Computer Vision* edited by Winston. The paper proposed the "Frame" data structure to describe stereotyped scenarios (like "entering a living room"), utilizing fixed information at the top and "slots" for specific instances at the bottom, which have default values that subframes can override. Together, these frames form a "frame system" that uses transformations to represent perspectives, actions, and causal relationships.
events.card_summary_en: Slot-and-default frames gave machines a new structure for scenes, objects, actions, and causes.
events.why_it_matters_en: Frames were the turning point in symbolic knowledge representation, upgrading atomic propositions plus predicate logic into composite structures carrying defaults, laying conceptual groundwork for the 1980s expert-system boom. Object-oriented programming, JSON Schema, Protobuf messages, and vector database schemas all bear Frame's imprint.
events.behind_scenes_en: The real contribution was less a data structure than defaults plus perspective shifting: Minsky wanted frames to explain how you know a living room probably holds a sofa before surveying the room. The paper itself admitted it poses a series of questions more than it supplies answers. Frames, Schank's Scripts of 1975, and Bobrow's KRL of 1977 were ranked the three schools of 1970s knowledge representation, and the object-oriented knowledge bases of 1980s expert systems largely grew from frame thinking, Minsky's Frame concept a distant relative of OOP class inheritance.

events.title_zh: Werbos 反向传播:深度学习的数学起点
events.title_en: Werbos Backpropagation: Beyond Regression (1974 Harvard PhD)
events.summary_zh:
1974 年 8 月,Paul Werbos 在哈佛大学通过博士论文答辩,题目《Beyond Regression: New Tools for Prediction and Analysis in the Behavioral Sciences》。
论文第二章首次完整提出用链式法则从输出端往输入端反推偏导,在多层复合函数里“一次正向 + 一次反向”算出所有参数的梯度,并明确指出这套方法可以训练多层神经网络。
这是 backpropagation 算法在西方文献中的首次完整描述。
events.source_name: Werbos, P. (1974). Harvard PhD thesis; (1994) Wiley book The Roots of Backpropagation
events.card_summary_zh: 这是 backpropagation 算法在西方文献中的首次完整描述；BP 是整个深度学习的训练算法基石。
events.summary_en: In August 1974, Paul Werbos defended his PhD thesis at Harvard University, titled *Beyond Regression: New Tools for Prediction and Analysis in the Behavioral Sciences*. In the second chapter, he proposed for the first time in its entirety the use of the chain rule to reverse-propagate partial derivatives from the output to the input, calculating the gradients of all parameters in a multi-layer composite function via "one forward and one backward" pass, and explicitly pointed out that this method could train multi-layer neural networks. This marked the first complete description of the backpropagation algorithm in Western literature.
events.card_summary_en: BP's first complete description in Western literature, the training cornerstone of deep learning.
events.why_it_matters_en: Backpropagation is deep learning's foundational training algorithm. Every training loop inside GPT, Claude, Gemini, Stable Diffusion, and AlphaFold is essentially Werbos 1974: predict forward, compute gradients backward, update weights. That BP lay buried for twelve years after 1974 explains why Hinton's generation treats being misunderstood as ordinary research weather.
events.behind_scenes_en: By Werbos's 1974 defense, neural networks were academic forbidden ground; Minsky and Papert's 1969 Perceptrons had condemned the road, and nobody on the committee believed networks could revive. Werbos himself mostly wielded the math as a general forecasting tool, applying it to political prediction and energy modeling. Only after Rumelhart, Hinton, and Williams independently re-derived BP in Nature in 1986 and fixed the name backpropagation was the 1974 paper retroactively recognized. Werbos later observed that Freud's 1895 Project for a Scientific Psychology had described a similar backward learning signal.

events.title_zh: MYCIN:专家系统进入医学诊断
events.title_en: MYCIN: Medical Expert System
events.summary_zh:
1974 年 10 月,Edward Shortliffe 在斯坦福提交博士论文《MYCIN: A Rule-Based Computer Program for Advising Physicians Regarding Antimicrobial Therapy Selection》(CS-TR-74-465, AIM-251)。
MYCIN 用 ~600 条产生式规则,把感染科医生判断菌血症、选抗生素的经验编码进 LISP 程序。
它最重要的一项创新是把确定性推理改造成“确定性因子(Certainty Factor)”,在规则之间传递部分置信度,这是当时不确定性推理的代表作。
1979 年 Yu 等人评估:MYCIN 的抗生素选择 65% 被专家评为可接受,高于 9 名人类住院医师的中位数(具体比例与对照人数待核实)。
events.source_name: Shortliffe, E. H. (1974). PhD thesis, Stanford CS-TR-74-465; (1975) Comput Biomed Res 8(4)
events.card_summary_zh: MYCIN 用数百条规则辅助诊断感染和选择抗生素，展示了专家知识如何被编码进一套可解释系统。
events.summary_en: In October 1974, Edward Shortliffe submitted his Stanford PhD dissertation, "MYCIN: A Rule-Based Computer Program for Advising Physicians Regarding Antimicrobial Therapy Selection" (CS-TR-74-465, AIM-251), introducing a LISP program that encoded infectious disease specialists' expertise in diagnosing bacteremia and selecting antibiotics into roughly 600 production rules. Its key innovation was adapting deterministic reasoning into "Certainty Factors" to propagate partial confidence between rules, serving as a landmark achievement in uncertainty reasoning for the era. In 1979, an evaluation by Yu et al. found that MYCIN's antibiotic selections were deemed acceptable by experts 65% of the time, outperforming the median of nine human residents (though the exact ratio and control count are pending verification).
events.card_summary_en: MYCIN encoded hundreds of rules to diagnose infections and choose antibiotics, explainably.
events.why_it_matters_en: MYCIN was AI's earliest serious attempt at medicine, pushing explicit encoding of expert knowledge to its limit while exposing the exploding maintenance cost of rule bases. Today's LLM-based clinical assistants take the statistical road, but the question of what responsibility AI carries in medicine was posed in MYCIN's day and remains unresolved.
events.behind_scenes_en: MYCIN never actually entered clinical use, blocked not by performance but by law, liability, and upkeep: who answers for a wrong recommendation, who pays to keep the rules current as antibiotics change. Shortliffe later reflected that its true contribution was not medicine but the template handed to EMYCIN in 1979, PROSPECTOR, XCON, and successors: knowledge base plus inference engine plus explanation module. EMYCIN also introduced the domain-independent shell concept, directly shaping the 1980s expert-system industry.

events.title_zh: Altair 8800:个人计算机革命起点
events.title_en: Altair 8800: Personal Computer Revolution Begins
events.summary_zh:
1974 年 12 月 19 日,《Popular Electronics》1975 年 1 月号上市,封面故事是 Ed Roberts 和 Bill Yates 设计的 Altair 8800 微型计算机套件,封面标题“World's First Minicomputer Kit to Rival Commercial Models”。
整机基于 Intel 8080,套件 439 美元,组装版 621 美元。
Roberts 原本预计卖出 800 台,上市后 1 个月内收到 1000 多订单,MITS 公司从破产边缘翻身。
events.source_name: Roberts, H. E. & Yates, W. (1975). Popular Electronics Jan 1975; Computing History
events.card_summary_zh: Altair 8800 把可编程计算机带给个人爱好者，并直接催生微软，个人计算机产业由此点火。
events.summary_en: On December 19, 1974, the January 1975 issue of *Popular Electronics* hit newsstands, featuring a cover story on the Altair 8800 microcomputer kit designed by Ed Roberts and Bill Yates under the headline "World's First Minicomputer Kit to Rival Commercial Models." Powered by the Intel 8080, the machine cost $439 as a kit and $621 fully assembled. While Roberts initially expected to sell just 800 units, over 1,000 orders flooded in within a month of its release, pulling MITS back from the brink of bankruptcy.
events.card_summary_en: Altair 8800 put programmable computers in hobbyists' hands and started Microsoft and the PC era.
events.why_it_matters_en: Altair 8800 was the starting gun of the personal computer industry, directly producing Microsoft, IMSAI, and the 1976 Apple I, along with the Homebrew Computer Club where Jobs and Wozniak found their inspiration for the Apple I. For AI it made personal computing industrially real, paving the first road toward compute as a household commodity.
events.behind_scenes_en: The machine on the magazine cover was an empty shell: the prototype assembled and mailed in October 1974 was lost to a freight strike, so MITS propped up a bare box with LEDs for the January 1975 cover shoot. Harvard sophomore Bill Gates and Paul Allen wrote Altair BASIC, Micro-Soft's first business. Afterward a crowd of clones from IMSAI, Processor Technology, and Ohio Scientific appeared, and the PC industrial chain was underway.

events.title_zh: Holland 遗传算法:把进化变成算法
events.title_en: Holland Genetic Algorithm: Adaptation in Natural and Artificial Systems
events.summary_zh:
1975 年,密歇根大学 John Holland 出版《Adaptation in Natural and Artificial Systems》,提出遗传算法(Genetic Algorithm)。
GA 把“候选解”编码成二进制串,通过选择、交叉、变异三步迭代,在解空间里做“适者生存”式搜索。
Holland 在书中给出 Schema Theorem,试图从信息论角度证明GA 的“building block”会指数级增长。
1975 年同期的博士 Ken De Jong 用 GA 做函数优化,给出 GA 的首批实验基准。
events.source_name: Holland, J. H. (1975). Adaptation in Natural and Artificial Systems. U. Michigan Press
events.card_summary_zh: 遗传算法把选择、交叉与变异写成搜索程序，让“适者生存”第一次成为机器解决复杂问题的方法。
events.summary_en: In 1975, the University of Michigan’s John Holland published *Adaptation in Natural and Artificial Systems*, introducing the Genetic Algorithm (GA) to encode "candidate solutions" as binary strings and perform a "survival of the fittest" search through selection, crossover, and mutation. In the book, Holland presented the Schema Theorem to prove from an information-theory perspective that GA "building blocks" grow exponentially, while Ken De Jong, a PhD student at the same time in 1975, used GA for function optimization to establish the algorithm's first experimental benchmarks.
events.card_summary_en: Genetic algorithms wrote selection, crossover, and mutation down as search procedures.
events.why_it_matters_en: GA gave adaptation, as a concept, its earliest formalization inside AI, shaping evolutionary computation, reinforcement learning, and neuroevolution. Neural architecture search in AutoML, the evolution strategies OpenAI used early on, and DeepMind's structure searches after AlphaFold all show GA's shadow.
events.behind_scenes_en: Holland's inspirations were Darwin, Turing, and von Neumann's self-replicating machines, driven by one question: is adaptation the same mathematical process in organisms and machines? Through the 1970s GA and BP ran on parallel tracks, GA on discrete combinatorial optimization, BP on differentiable continuous optimization, hardly speaking. In the 1980s Holland's student Goldberg published Genetic Algorithms in Search, carrying GA into industry, where scheduling, structural design, and network-architecture search still use it routinely.

events.title_zh: 物理符号系统假说:Newell & Simon Turing 演讲
events.title_en: Physical Symbol System Hypothesis (Newell & Simon 1975 Turing Lecture)
events.summary_zh:
1975 年 10 月 20 日,Allen Newell 和 Herbert A. Simon 在明尼阿波利斯 ACM 年会上联合接受 1975 年 ACM Turing Award,演讲题为《Computer Science as Empirical Inquiry:Symbols and Search》,1976 年 3 月发表于 CACM 19(3)。
演讲正式提出物理符号系统假说(PSSH):“一个物理符号系统具备产生一般智能行为的必要和充分手段”。
他们把过去 20 年 Logic Theorist、GPS、NSS 的工作总结为两条原则:智能 = 符号操作 + 启发式搜索。
这是符号主义 AI 最完整的纲领性陈述。
events.source_name: Newell, A. & Simon, H. A. (1976). CACM 19(3):113-126
events.card_summary_zh: 演讲正式提出物理符号系统假说(PSSH):“一个物理符号系统具备产生一般智能行为的必要和充分手段”；PSSH 是符号主义的“宪法”。
events.summary_en: On October 20, 1975, Allen Newell and Herbert A. Simon jointly accepted the 1975 ACM Turing Award at the ACM Annual Conference in Minneapolis, delivering the lecture "Computer Science as Empirical Inquiry: Symbols and Search," which was published in March 1976 in CACM 19(3). The address formally proposed the Physical Symbol System Hypothesis (PSSH): "A physical symbol system has the necessary and sufficient means for general intelligent action." By summarizing the past 20 years of work on the Logic Theorist, GPS, and NSS into two principles—intelligence equals symbol manipulation plus heuristic search—they delivered the most complete programmatic statement of symbolic AI.
events.card_summary_en: Newell and Simon's Turing lecture declared symbol systems capable of general intelligent action.
events.why_it_matters_en: PSSH is symbolism's constitution, concentrating 1970s-80s AI effort on search, knowledge representation, and inference engines. Brooks's 1985 broadside for intelligence without representation, connectionism's 1990s revival, and the deep learning surge of the 2010s were all rebellions against it. Without understanding PSSH you cannot tell what each AI paradigm revolution was actually rejecting.
events.behind_scenes_en: Simon also collected the 1978 Nobel memorial prize in economics for bounded rationality, the only person ever to hold both a Turing Award and a Nobel. In the lecture Newell pressed the claim that computer science is an empirical discipline: AI cannot advance by pure mathematical derivation but must build machines, write programs, run experiments, and examine results. That stance stood then against Dijkstra's computer-science-as-mathematics, and deep learning's experience-driven research paradigm today is the Newell-Simon line carried forward.

events.title_zh: Lenat AM:机器自动做数学发现
events.title_en: Lenat AM: Automated Mathematical Discovery
events.summary_zh:
1975-1976 年,Douglas Lenat 在斯坦福完成博士论文《AM: An Artificial Intelligence Approachto Discovery in Mathematics》。
AM 用 ~250 个 Lisp 概念和 ~500 条启发式规则,从空集和集合论公理出发,自动“重新发现”了整数、加法、素数、唯一分解定理等数论概念。
AM 不会证明定理,但能“提出有趣的新概念并给评分”。
这是 AI 史上第一个被认真讨论的“自动发现系统”。
events.source_name: Lenat, D. (1976). Stanford PhD; (1977) IJCAI; (1982) Artificial Intelligence 21(1-2)
events.card_summary_zh: AM 从少量概念和启发式规则出发重新发现数学规律，成为机器参与科学发现的早期大胆实验。
events.summary_en: In 1975-1976, Douglas Lenat completed his Stanford PhD thesis, *AM: An Artificial Intelligence Approach to Discovery in Mathematics*. Using ~250 Lisp concepts and ~500 heuristic rules, AM started from the empty set and set theory axioms to automatically "rediscover" number theory concepts like integers, addition, prime numbers, and the unique factorization theorem. Although unable to prove theorems, it could "propose interesting new concepts and score them," marking it as the first "automated discovery system" to be seriously discussed in the history of AI.
events.card_summary_en: From a few concepts and heuristics, AM rediscovered mathematical patterns on its own.
events.why_it_matters_en: AM was AI's earliest automatic-scientific-discovery experiment, leaving the generate-concepts-plus-heuristic-evaluation frame to Graffiti in 1988, Colton's HR in 1999, and DeepMind's AlphaTensor in 2022 and FunSearch in 2023. Its successes and disputes frame AI for Science's central tension: does AI discover new things, or only extend human presets?
events.behind_scenes_en: The triumph quickly drew suspicion. In 1984 Ritchie and Hanna published AM: A Case Study in AI Methodology in Artificial Intelligence volume 23 number 3, pages 249-268, showing AM's discoveries had been quietly fed in by Lenat through Lisp function naming and heuristics, with every generated prime traceable to Lenat's own divisor-of rule. Lenat later conceded the heuristic evaluations were hand-tuned and pivoted to founding Cyc in 1984, explicitly encoding common sense, a project now forty years old. The dispute remains the reference case for whether discovery systems produce genuine novelty or only amplify their author's preset search directions.

events.title_zh: Apple II:个人计算机走入家庭
events.title_en: Apple II: Personal Computer Goes Consumer
events.summary_zh:
1977 年 4 月,Steve Wozniak 设计的 Apple II 在 West Coast Computer Faire 首次公开展示;6 月 10 日开始正式发售,起价 1298 美元。
Apple II 是第一款大规模商业成功的“开箱即用”个人电脑:主板 + 键盘 + 电源整合在塑料壳内,直接接家用电视当显示器,内置 BASIC 解释器,普通家庭就能上手。
1978 年 5.25 英寸软盘驱动器(DOS 3.1)推出,1980 年 VisiCalc 表格程序上市,Apple II 进入企业市场。
events.source_name: Wozniak, S. (1977) Apple II Reference Manual; Apple Inc. history
events.card_summary_zh: Apple II：个人计算机走入家庭；Apple II 让个人电脑从“极客玩具”变成“家用设备”。
events.summary_en: In April 1977, the Steve Wozniak-designed Apple II made its public debut at the West Coast Computer Faire, officially going on sale on June 10 at a starting price of $1,298. It became the first mass-market, commercially successful "out-of-the-box" personal computer, integrating a motherboard, keyboard, and power supply into a plastic case that plugged directly into a home TV and featured a built-in BASIC interpreter for ordinary families. The system broke into the enterprise market following the launch of a 5.25-inch floppy disk drive (DOS 3.1) in 1978 and the VisiCalc spreadsheet program in 1980.
events.card_summary_en: Apple II carried personal computers from hobbyist kits into family homes.
events.why_it_matters_en: Apple II turned the personal computer from a geek toy into a household appliance. For AI that meant computing entered homes and schools at scale, laying the hardware base for anyone-can-program in the 1980s-90s. Hinton's 1986 BP paper and LeCun's 1989 LeNet experiments both presupposed compute an ordinary researcher could buy and take home.
events.behind_scenes_en: Designing the Apple II, Wozniak still worked at HP and offered it there first; HP declined, citing no market for personal computers. Jobs sold his minivan, Woz sold his HP-65 calculator, and together they scraped 1,300 dollars for the first board. Its ready-to-run, fully assembled approach split decisively from the Altair 8800's solder-it-yourself kit route of 1975, defining the PC's commercial template. By the 1980s Apple IIs filled over a million seats in American schools, the entry machine for a generation of programmers and AI researchers.

events.title_zh: Anderson BPS:神经联想记忆早期模型
events.title_en: Anderson BPS: Brain-State-in-a-Box Associative Memory
events.summary_zh:
1977 年 7 月,James Anderson、Jack Silverstein、Stephen Ritz、Richard Jones 在Psychological Review 84(5) 发表《Distinctive Features, Categorical Perception,and Probability Learning: Some Applications of a Neural Model》。
提出 BPS 模型,后称 Brain-State-in-a-Box(BSB),用线性联想记忆 + 反馈 + 阈值函数,让向量在“盒子”里收敛到一个角点,实现“自动补全 / 类别收敛”。
这是 70 年代少数仍坚持神经路线的工作之一。
events.source_name: Anderson, Silverstein, Ritz, Jones (1977). Psychological Review 84(5):413-451
events.card_summary_zh: Anderson BPS：神经联想记忆早期模型；BPS 是连接主义在第一次寒冬里“地下存活”的代表。
events.summary_en: In July 1977, James Anderson, Jack Silverstein, Stephen Ritz, and Richard Jones published "Distinctive Features, Categorical Perception, and Probability Learning: Some Applications of a Neural Model" in *Psychological Review* 84(5). The paper introduced the BPS model, later known as Brain-State-in-a-Box (BSB), which used linear associative memory, feedback, and a threshold function to force vectors to converge to a corner inside the "box" to achieve "auto-completion / categorical convergence." It stood as one of the few research efforts during the 1970s that kept the neural network approach alive.
events.card_summary_en: Anderson's brain-state-in-a-box, an associative memory keeping connectionism alive underground.
events.why_it_matters_en: BPS is the emblem of connectionism surviving underground through the first winter. Alongside Kohonen's 1972 associative memory, Nakano's 1972 Associatron, and Fukushima's 1975 Neocognitron, it proved neural network research never truly died, only went marginalized. After Hopfield's 1982 paper the line revived fast, and Rumelhart-Hinton-Williams's 1986 backpropagation carried it to LeCun, Hinton, and Bengio's next starting point.
events.behind_scenes_en: Neural network research was quiet money in the 1970s, and Anderson and peers secured funding under cognitive psychology banners rather than AI ones. BPS and BSB are not Hopfield networks but kin in spirit: a feedback dynamical system attracting memories toward stable points. Hopfield's 1982 paper explicitly cited contemporaries Anderson, Kohonen, and Nakano, and looking back, those marginal late-70s works preserved the thread that Hopfield's revival picked up directly in 1982.

events.title_zh: PROSPECTOR:专家系统找到矿
events.title_en: PROSPECTOR: Expert System for Mineral Exploration
events.summary_zh:
1976-1980 年,Peter Hart、Richard Duda、Nils Nilsson 在 SRI International 开发 PROSPECTOR,用于辅助地质学家评估矿藏潜力。
1977 年 10 月 20 日 SRI Technical Note 155 公开发表首版系统。
PROSPECTOR 用“推理网络(inference network)”编码地质学家的判断,节点是地质断言,边是 Bayesian 概率传递。
1980 年 PROSPECTOR 推测华盛顿州 Mount Tolman 存在大型钼矿,后续钻探证实了预测,这是 AI 史上首次重大“商业级”预测成功案例。
events.source_name: Duda, Hart, Nilsson et al. (1977) SRI TN-155; (1978) SRI Final Report
events.card_summary_zh: 1977 年 10 月 20 日 SRI Technical Note 155 公开发表首版系统。
events.summary_en: Between 1976 and 1980, Peter Hart, Richard Duda, and Nils Nilsson at SRI International developed PROSPECTOR to assist geologists in assessing mineral potential, with the system's first version publicly released in SRI Technical Note 155 on October 20, 1977. The system used an "inference network" to encode geological expertise, utilizing nodes for geological assertions and edges for Bayesian probability propagation. In 1980, PROSPECTOR predicted a massive molybdenum deposit at Mount Tolman in Washington State, which subsequent drilling confirmed, marking the first major "commercial-grade" predictive success in AI history.
events.card_summary_en: SRI's Technical Note 155 published the system's first version on October 20, 1977.
events.why_it_matters_en: PROSPECTOR ranked among the expert-system era's killer applications, and with MYCIN, DENDRAL, and XCON it pushed AI from laboratory into industry and government. It also opened the probabilistic-reasoning-plus-knowledge-graph line that today's Bayesian networks, probabilistic graphical models, and causal inference tools all trace back to.
events.behind_scenes_en: The core technology was not rules but Bayesian probability propagation. Duda, Hart, Nilsson, and Pearl jointly advanced computable representations of uncertainty in the late 1970s, with PROSPECTOR the first industrial-grade deployment of that line. The Mount Tolman ore-prediction legend gets cited endlessly, though the commercial value of the drilled vein stayed contested. Afterward Duda and Hart's textbook era and Pearl's 1988 Probabilistic Reasoning in Intelligent Systems made Bayesian networks one of 1990s AI's mainstreams.

events.title_zh: Lamport 提出逻辑时钟——分布式系统的基石
events.title_en: Lamport's Logical Clocks
events.summary_zh: 1978 年，莱斯利·兰伯特发表论文《分布式系统中的时间、时钟与事件排序》。他证明了独立计算机之间不存在统一的「现在」——并提出用因果关系的「先发生于」替代物理时间。
events.source_name: Fireship - 10 Classic CS Papers
events.card_summary_zh: 他证明了独立计算机之间不存在统一的「现在」——并提出用因果关系的「先发生于」替代物理时间。
events.summary_en: In 1978, Leslie Lamport published his paper "Time, Clocks, and the Ordering of Events in a Distributed System." He proved that a unified "now" does not exist between independent computers, proposing instead to replace physical time with a causal "happened-before" relationship.
events.card_summary_en: No shared now exists across computers, so causality must replace physical time, Lamport showed.
events.why_it_matters_en: Without logical clocks there are no distributed databases and no synchronized training of large models across thousands of GPUs. Every cloud service you touch, every blockchain transaction, every distributed AI training run rests underneath on this paper.
events.behind_scenes_en: Lamport's insight was simple: if A may cause B to happen, treat A as occurring before B. That seemingly plain idea cracked one of computer science's nastiest synchronization problems, letting dozens or thousands of machines with private clocks agree without sharing a global clock. Training GPT-class models now demands tens of thousands of GPUs in parallel, and logical clocks are the mathematics keeping their steps in line.

events.title_zh: 西蒙获诺贝尔经济学奖：唯一同时拿图灵奖和诺贝尔奖的人
events.title_en: Herbert Simon Wins Nobel Prize in Economics
events.summary_zh:
1978 年 10 月 16 日，瑞典皇家科学院宣布将当年诺贝尔经济学奖授予赫伯特·西蒙，表彰他对经济组织决策过程的开创性研究。
西蒙提出的「有限理性」（Bounded Rationality）和「满意即可」（Satisficing）颠覆了传统经济学的完全理性假设。他指出：人在决策时信息有限、认知有限、时间有限，因此只会追求「够好」的方案而非「最优」方案。
这个思想为行为经济学奠基，也深刻影响了管理学和组织理论。
西蒙 1975 年已与纽厄尔共同获得图灵奖。他至今仍是历史上唯一同时获得图灵奖和诺贝尔奖的人。
events.source_name: Nobel Prize Official Website: Herbert A. Simon
events.card_summary_zh: 西蒙获诺贝尔经济学奖：唯一同时拿图灵奖和诺贝尔奖的人；诺贝尔奖的意义不止于西蒙个人。
events.summary_en: On October 16, 1978, the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences awarded the Nobel Prize in Economics to Herbert Simon for his pioneering research into the decision-making processes within economic organizations. Simon’s concepts of "Bounded Rationality" and "Satisficing" upended traditional economics' assumption of perfect rationality by showing that humans, constrained by limited information, cognition, and time, seek "good enough" rather than "optimal" solutions—a breakthrough that laid the foundation for behavioral economics and deeply influenced management and organizational theory. Having already co-won the Turing Award with Newell in 1975, Simon remains the only person in history to win both the Turing Award and the Nobel Prize.
events.card_summary_en: Simon took the economics Nobel, the only person ever to hold both it and the Turing Award.
events.why_it_matters_en: The Nobel counted for more than Simon personally. It certified that AI research results, symbolic operation, heuristic search, bounded rationality, could spill beyond computing into genuine influence on economics and management. AI touching nearly every discipline today finds its earliest evidence here.
events.behind_scenes_en: Simon's cross-field path dazzles: political science doctor, then chairs in administration and economics, ending atop psychology and computer science. Behind the prize lies a neglected link: studying organizational decision-making at Carnegie Mellon really meant studying how humans optimize under limited resources, a framing that directly yielded bounded rationality and heuristic search. His Logic Theorist and GPS in AI simulated human problem-solving all along, his economics and AI research sharing one problem framework.

events.title_zh: Hofstadter《哥德尔、艾舍尔、巴赫》出版
events.title_en: Hofstadter GEB: An Eternal Golden Braid
events.summary_zh:
1979 年,Douglas Hofstadter 出版《Gödel, Escher, Bach: An Eternal Golden Braid》(Basic Books,777 页)。
书中通过哥德尔不完备定理、艾舍尔版画、巴赫赋格三个表面无关的领域,提取出共同结构“怪圈(Strange Loop)”:自指、层次缠绕、递归回旋。
Hofstadter 论证“意识”可能源于符号系统达到足够复杂度后的怪圈结构。
1980 年该书获普利策非小说类奖和美国国家图书奖(科学类)。
events.source_name: Hofstadter, D. R. (1979). Gödel, Escher, Bach. Basic Books. ISBN 0-465-02656-7
events.card_summary_zh: Hofstadter《哥德尔、艾舍尔、巴赫》出版；GEB 是 AI 与认知科学交界处影响最大的非教材书。
events.summary_en: In 1979, Douglas Hofstadter published *Gödel, Escher, Bach: An Eternal Golden Braid* (Basic Books, 777 pages), extracting a common structure called the "Strange Loop"—defined by self-reference, tangled hierarchies, and recursive looping—from the seemingly unrelated domains of Gödel's incompleteness theorem, Escher's prints, and Bach's fugues. Hofstadter argued that "consciousness" might emerge from these strange loop structures once a symbolic system reaches sufficient complexity. In 1980, the book won the Pulitzer Prize for General Nonfiction and the National Book Award (Science).
events.card_summary_en: Gödel, Escher, Bach appeared, the most influential non-textbook at AI's frontier.
events.why_it_matters_en: GEB loaded self-reference, emergence, levels, and formal systems into a generation of researchers' toolboxes. Today's arguments over whether LLMs understand, whether consciousness can emerge from Transformers, whether self-referential loops can produce a self, all turn within GEB's conceptual frame.
events.behind_scenes_en: Hofstadter was just past thirty, fresh from an Oregon physics doctorate and teaching at Indiana, when he wrote it. He complained for years afterward that the public filed GEB as a math-art-music popularization while his real target was how consciousness emerges from lifeless matter. It shaped a generation of AI researchers: his student Melanie Mitchell went on to Copycat, and DeepMind founder Demis Hassabis openly credits GEB as a key enlightenment. Critics charged it substituted analogy for proof, and Hofstadter granted part of the criticism in his 1999 twentieth-anniversary preface.

events.title_zh: Stanford Cart:5 小时穿越房间
events.title_en: Stanford Cart: 5-Hour Room Crossing
events.summary_zh:
