In 1959, his student Steve Russell read the draft, realized that "eval" could actually be run, and coded McCarthy's paper-based pseudocode into the IBM 704 to create Lisp's first working interpreter, prior to the paper’s official publication in the Communications of the ACM in April 1960.
timeline.card_summary_en: When Steve Russell read the paper and said eval could run directly, AI got its native tongue.
timeline.why_it_matters_en: Lisp is the most important language in AI history. Code as data, garbage collection, higher-order functions, REPLs, macros, closures: nearly every core feature of modern programming languages comes from Lisp, a debt Python, JavaScript, Ruby, Rust, Clojure, and Julia are still repaying. More crucially, Lisp's meta-circular eval directly inspired Prolog interpreters, 1970s expert-system shells, and the token-by-token decoding of 2010s LLMs, wherever programs manipulate programs.
timeline.behind_scenes_en: In History of Lisp, his 1979 Stanford account, McCarthy recalled two key accidents in Lisp's birth. The first was S-expressions: he originally designed M-expressions resembling FORTRAN, but they proved hard to parse, forcing him to adopt nested-parenthesis S-expressions as the underlying representation, which turned out naturally isomorphic to syntax trees and became Lisp's core advantage. The second was garbage collection: the early IBM 704 had only 32K words of memory, list objects were constantly allocated and freed, and manual management invited errors, so McCarthy invented mark-and-sweep collection, the first systematic proposal of garbage collection in computer science. He also designed the Advice Taker, a program holding common sense as logical statements and reasoning from them, illustrated by telling the machine birds fly so it infers sparrows fly unless told penguins do not.

timeline.title_zh: McCarthy Advice Taker 提案：用逻辑让机器推理常识
timeline.title_en: McCarthy's Advice Taker Proposal
timeline.summary_zh:
1958 年 12 月，John McCarthy 在 MIT AI Memo #2 发表《Programs with Common Sense》，提出 Advice Taker 设想——一个"被告知常识后能自己推理"的程序。
他的核心例子：告诉机器"鸟会飞"，它就应推出"麻雀会飞"，除非你告诉它"企鹅不会飞"。
Advice Taker 不需要为每个新事实重写程序，而是用一阶逻辑+推理引擎自动推出结论。
timeline.source_name: McCarthy, J. (1958). Programs with Common Sense. MIT AI Memo #2. In Proceedings of the Teddington Conference on the Mechanization of Thought Processes (1959).
timeline.card_summary_zh: Advice Taker 不需要为每个新事实重写程序，而是用一阶逻辑+推理引擎自动推出结论。
timeline.summary_en: In December 1958, John McCarthy published "Programs with Common Sense" in MIT AI Memo #2, proposing the "Advice Taker"—a program designed to reason on its own after being told common sense. His core example was simple: tell the machine "birds can fly," and it should deduce "sparrows can fly," unless told "penguins cannot fly." Rather than requiring a rewrite for every new fact, the Advice Taker would use first-order logic and an inference engine to automatically derive conclusions.
timeline.card_summary_en: Advice Taker would reason about common sense from logic, no reprogramming for each new fact.
timeline.why_it_matters_en: Advice Taker was the first declarative-AI proposal, directly informing Alain Colmerauer's Prolog in 1972, Douglas Lenat's Cyc from 1984, and today's prompt engineering, since an LLM system prompt is essentially the advice McCarthy imagined. Until his death in 2011, McCarthy's final paper still asked what common sense is and how to give it to machines.
timeline.behind_scenes_en: McCarthy was writing Lisp at the time and intended Advice Taker as a layer above Lisp that spoke logic, but with Lisp still immature it remained a paper proposal. Colmerauer realized the idea as Prolog in Marseille in 1972, and Japan's Fifth Generation Computer project chose Prolog as its strategic language in the 1980s, ultimately failing. The Cyc project invested roughly 2,000 person-years from 1984 to 2024 hand-coding millions of common-sense items without reaching McCarthy's vision. Only in the 2020s did LLMs surface common-sense ability through pretraining and instruction tuning, partially solving Advice Taker's core problem statistically rather than through the logic McCarthy envisioned, a sixty-five-year detour and the largest paradigm war in AI history.

timeline.title_zh: Hubel-Wiesel 发现视觉皮层简单/复杂细胞：CNN 的生物学源头
timeline.title_en: Hubel and Wiesel Discover Simple and Complex Cells in Cat Striate Cortex
timeline.summary_zh:
1958 年春，David Hubel 从 Walter Reed Army Institute 跳槽到 Johns Hopkins Hospital Stephen Kuffler 实验室，与同实验室的 Torsten Wiesel 开始合作。
原计划只合作 9 个月（Hubel 等 Mountcastle 实验室装修），结果合作延续 25 年。
他们用钨丝微电极记录猫初级视觉皮层（V1/striate cortex）单细胞放电，意外发现：神经元的最佳刺激不是"光点"（如视网膜和 LGN 那样），而是"特定朝向的亮边或暗条"。
1959 年他们在《Journal of Physiology》发表《Receptive fields of single neurones in the cat's striate cortex》（148(3), 574-591），首次报告 simple cell 概念；
1962 年同一期刊发表《Receptive fields, binocular interaction and functional architecture in the cat's visual cortex》（160, 106-154），系统定义 simple cell 和 complex cell 两类神经元，并提出层级模型：simple cell 接收 LGN 输入聚合形成方向选择性，complex cell 接收 simple cell 输入形成位置不变性。
1981 年两人与 Roger Sperry 共同获得诺贝尔生理学或医学奖。
timeline.source_name: Hubel, D. H., Wiesel, T. N. (1959). Receptive fields of single neurones in the cat's striate cortex. J. Physiology, 148(3), 574-591.
timeline.card_summary_zh: 他们用钨丝微电极记录猫初级视觉皮层（V1/striate cortex）单细胞放电，意外发现。
timeline.summary_en: In the spring of 1958, David Hubel left the Walter Reed Army Institute for Stephen Kuffler's lab at Johns Hopkins Hospital, teaming up with Torsten Wiesel for what was supposed to be a nine-month stint during Mountcastle's lab renovation, but turned into a 25-year collaboration. Using tungsten microelectrodes to record single-cell discharges in the cat's primary visual cortex (V1/striate cortex), they accidentally discovered that the optimal stimulus for neurons was not "spots of light" (as in the retina and LGN), but rather "oriented light edges or dark bars." This work led to a 1959 *Journal of Physiology* paper (148(3), 574-591) first reporting the "simple cell" concept, followed by a 1962 paper in the same journal (160, 106-154) that systematically defined simple and complex cells and proposed a hierarchical model—where simple cells pool LGN inputs to form orientation selectivity, and complex cells pool simple cell inputs to achieve position invariance—ultimately earning the duo, alongside Roger Sperry, the 1981 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
timeline.card_summary_en: Recordings from cat visual cortex uncovered simple and complex cells, CNN's biological source.
timeline.why_it_matters_en: Hubel and Wiesel's hierarchical receptive-field model directly inspired Kunihiko Fukushima's Neocognitron in 1980, the first network with convolution plus pooling structure, itself the direct predecessor of Yann LeCun's LeNet in 1989, the first successful CNN. Today conv layers correspond to simple cells and pooling layers to complex cells, one of the rare cases in AI history of neuroscience directly driving engineering. Attention heads' orientation selectivity in ImageNet-era models, ResNets, and ViTs all trace back to Hubel and Wiesel in 1959.
timeline.behind_scenes_en: The first simple-cell discovery was a late-night accident in 1958: projecting dots of light onto a screen before a cat, they had a microelectrode in a V1 neuron but could not provoke any response. In frustration Hubel pushed a glass slide with a square hole into the light path, its edge cast a moving shadow on the screen, and the loudspeaker suddenly burst into machine-gun-like firing. They realized V1 neurons ignore dots of light and care only about edges and bars of specific orientation. Hubel recalled in his 1981 Nobel lecture that it was a wonderfully exciting time and we both knew we were on to something big. Their hierarchical model was vastly exceeded by deep learning in the 2010s, with stacks of conv layers far more complex than V1, but hierarchy plus receptive fields plus invariance remain the unchanged core ideas.

timeline.title_zh: Gelernter 几何定理证明器：图搜索+反向推理的早期样板
timeline.title_en: Gelernter's Geometry Theorem Prover
timeline.summary_zh:
1959 年，Herbert Gelernter 在 IBM Watson Research Center完成几何定理证明器（Geometry Theorem Prover, GTP），用 FLPL（FORTRAN List Processing Language）在 IBM 704 上实现。
GTP 给定一个几何命题（如"等腰三角形底角相等"），会用反向推理+符号坐标代数生成证明步骤，并用" diagram "——一张根据命题画的示意图——快速剪掉那些在图上明显不成立的子目标。
这是历史上第一个用"视觉/几何直觉"辅助逻辑推理的程序。
timeline.source_name: Gelernter, H. (1959). Realization of a geometry-theorem proving machine. In Proceedings of the International Conference on Information Processing, 273-282.
timeline.card_summary_zh: GTP 给定一个几何命题（如"等腰三角形底角相等"），会用反向推理+符号坐标代数生成证明步骤。
timeline.summary_en: In 1959, Herbert Gelernter completed the Geometry Theorem Prover (GTP) at the IBM Watson Research Center, implementing it in FLPL (FORTRAN List Processing Language) on an IBM 704. Given a geometric proposition (such as "base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal"), GTP generated proof steps using backward reasoning and symbolic coordinate algebra, utilizing a "diagram"—a schematic drawn based on the proposition—to quickly prune subgoals that were obviously false on the diagram. This was the first program in history to use "visual/geometric intuition" to aid logical reasoning.
timeline.card_summary_en: GTP proved geometry theorems by combining backward reasoning with symbolic coordinate algebra.
timeline.why_it_matters_en: Given a geometric proposition such as equal base angles in an isosceles triangle, GTP generated proof steps by backward reasoning plus symbolic coordinate algebra. Beyond Newell and Simon's GPS, it was the earliest template of the other theorem-proving route, introducing diagram-based heuristic pruning, an idea recurring in 1980s expert systems, 1990s multimodal reasoning, and today's LLM visual chain-of-thought. Gelernter thereby became one of McCarthy's earliest Lisp students, advancing the early Lisp ecosystem with Steve Russell and Marvin Minsky.
timeline.behind_scenes_en: Gelernter's father was the noted painter; he himself originally studied physics before McCarthy recruited him to IBM's summer project to develop FLPL. Choosing geometry was pragmatic: Whitehead and Russell's Principia was already claimed by Logic Theorist, geometry offered abundant axiomatic sources in Euclid and Hilbert's 1899 Foundations of Geometry, and the property that drawing a figure reveals whether a proof works suited heuristic pruning perfectly. On an IBM 704, GTP proved the Pons Asinorum, equal base angles in an isosceles triangle, in six minutes, faster than the era's high schoolers. In the 1960s Gelernter moved into computer graphics; his son David became a Yale computer science professor wounded by the Unabomber in 1993, another story entirely.

timeline.title_zh: MIT Artificial Intelligence Project 启动：MIT AI 实验室的源点
timeline.title_en: MIT Artificial Intelligence Project Founded
timeline.summary_zh:
1959 年，John McCarthy 和 Marvin Minsky 在 MIT 共同组建 Artificial Intelligence Project，这是 MIT AI Lab 的最初形态（1963 年并入 MAC Project，1968 年 MAC Project 拆分出独立的 MIT AI Lab，2003 年与 LCS 合并为 CSAIL）。
项目初期由 McCarthy 担任主任，1962 年 McCarthy 离开 MIT 去 Stanford 创办 SAIL 后由 Minsky 接任。
项目最早成员包括 Steve Russell（Lisp 第一个解释器作者）、Bill Gosper、Richard Greenblatt（MacHack 作者）、Joel Moses 等。
timeline.source_name: Winston, P. H. (1981). MIT AI Lab: The First 25 Years (AIM-700).
timeline.card_summary_zh: MIT Artificial Intelligence Project 启动：MIT AI 实验室的源点。
timeline.summary_en: In 1959, John McCarthy and Marvin Minsky co-founded the Artificial Intelligence Project at MIT, the earliest incarnation of the MIT AI Lab, which merged into the MAC Project in 1963, spun out as an independent lab in 1968, and merged with LCS in 2003 to form CSAIL. McCarthy initially served as director until 1962, when he left MIT for Stanford to found SAIL, handing the reins to Minsky. The project’s earliest members included Steve Russell (author of the first Lisp interpreter), Bill Gosper, Richard Greenblatt (creator of MacHack), and Joel Moses, among others.
timeline.card_summary_en: The launch of MIT's AI Project, seed of the MIT AI Lab and of AI's institutional legitimacy.
timeline.why_it_matters_en: The MIT AI Project was the world's first university research unit named Artificial Intelligence, establishing the discipline's institutional legitimacy. It also fixed AI lab culture, overnight programming, the hack ethic, rule by technical merit, students knowing more than professors, and experimenting on the machines themselves, where early Lisp Machines, the PDP-6/10, and the ITS operating system were born. Stanford SAIL, CMU, and Xerox PARC copied the culture, and it fed Silicon Valley hacker culture, with large parts of Steven Levy's 1984 Hackers drawn from the MIT AI Lab.
timeline.behind_scenes_en: In 1959 MIT still had reservations about the very phrase Artificial Intelligence, initial funding was 10,000 dollars, and the office sat in Building 26, a small attic floor pending verification. McCarthy's real goal was a laboratory running around the clock, since the IBM 704 at MIT's Computation Center took daytime reservations only, forcing AI researchers to crowd into night-shift hack time. In 1962 McCarthy left for Stanford after MIT declined to elevate the Project into a department, compounded by long-standing tension with Minsky over direction, McCarthy leaning to logic and common sense, Minsky to neural networks and cognition, and founded the Stanford AI Lab. Minsky took over the MIT AI Project, folding it into the MAC Project in 1963.

timeline.title_zh: Samuel《Some Studies in Machine Learning Using the Game of Checkers》："Machine Learning" 一词的首次学术定义
timeline.title_en: Samuel Coins "Machine Learning" in IBM Journal
timeline.summary_zh:
1959 年 7 月，Arthur Samuel 在《IBM Journal of Research and Development》第 3 卷第 3 期发表《Some Studies in Machine Learning Using the Game of Checkers》（pp. 210-229）。
这是 "Machine Learning" 一词首次以学术方式正式使用，后人常用"让计算机在未被显式编程的情况下学习"来概括 Samuel 的思想（此句为转述，非论文原文逐字）；Samuel 论文中的真实表述是"a computer can be programmed so that it will learn to play a better game of checkers than can be played by the person who wrote the program"。
论文系统描述了跳棋程序的两类学习：rote learning（记棋谱）和 learning by generalization（参数学习），后者实质上就是后来 Sutton & Barto 在《Reinforcement Learning》中定义的 temporal-difference learning。
timeline.source_name: Samuel, A. L. (1959). Some Studies in Machine Learning Using the Game of Checkers. IBM Journal of Research and Development, 3(3), 210-229.
timeline.card_summary_zh: 这是 "Machine Learning" 一词首次以学术方式正式使用；篇论文不只首次定义了 machine learning 这个学科名。
timeline.summary_en: In July 1959, Arthur Samuel published "Some Studies in Machine Learning Using the Game of Checkers" in the *IBM Journal of Research and Development* (Vol. 3, No. 3, pp. 210-229), marking the first formal academic use of the term "Machine Learning." While his concept is frequently paraphrased today as enabling computers to learn without being explicitly programmed, Samuel's original text stated that "a computer can be programmed so that it will learn to play a better game of checkers than can be played by the person who wrote the program." The paper systematically described two types of learning for the checkers program: "rote learning" and "learning by generalization," the latter of which was essentially the "temporal-difference learning" later defined by Sutton & Barto in *Reinforcement Learning*.
timeline.card_summary_en: The first academic use of machine learning, and proof self-play can exceed its creator.
timeline.why_it_matters_en: The paper not only first defined machine learning as a subject name but first proved a machine could train beyond its programmer through self-play: Samuel's program beat self-styled checkers master Robert Nealey in one game in 1962, promoted heavily by IBM though Nealey was visually impaired rather than a top player and lost the rematch the next year, and Samuel judged that the program could now play a better game of checkers than the person who wrote it. That claim directly foreshadows AlphaGo Zero surpassing human knowledge through self-play in 2017. Tom Mitchell cited this paper when defining ML in his 1997 textbook.
timeline.behind_scenes_en: Samuel pushed the phrase machine learning partly to distinguish himself from cybernetics, held by Wiener, and artificial intelligence, held by McCarthy. His position at IBM was unusual: a Dartmouth participant long outside the three great AI centers of MIT, CMU, and Stanford. He chose checkers, a seemingly small domain, and cultivated it for thirty years precisely to show that machine learning does not require solving AGI first, that focused training in one domain reaches expert level. His alpha-beta pruning, independently proposed around the same time as Newell, Simon, and Shaw with priority still disputed, and temporal-difference learning, formally named by Sutton's 1988 paper, became twin cornerstones of reinforcement learning.

timeline.title_zh: NASA「人在环中」之争:Mercury 宇航员 vs 自动控制
timeline.title_en: NASA Human-in-the-Loop Debate (Mercury Program)
timeline.summary_zh:
1961 年,NASA 在 Mercury 计划中面临路线之争:工程师主张全自动飞行(“宇航员是乘客”),宇航员(来自试飞员背景)强烈反对,要求手工操纵权。
最终 Mercury-Atlas 6 (John Glenn, 1962-02-20) 采用“自动为主、人工接管”的混合方案,奠定了之后 Apollo、Gemini、航天飞机的人机协作范式。
这场争论确立了“human-in-the-loop”作为航天控制的核心原则,也间接催生了 1960 年代后期的“人机交互”作为独立学科。
timeline.source_name: NASA Mercury Program records, 1961-1963
timeline.card_summary_zh: NASA「人在环中」之争：Mercury 宇航员 vs 自动控制；场争论定义了“机器该听人的还是人该听机器的”这个至今未解的问题。
timeline.summary_en: In 1961, NASA faced a philosophical rift during Project Mercury: engineers advocated for fully automated flight (treating astronauts as "passengers"), while the astronauts, drawing on their test-pilot backgrounds, fiercely fought for manual control. The compromise came with Mercury-Atlas 6 (John Glenn, 1962-02-20), which adopted a hybrid "primarily automatic, manual takeover" approach that defined the human-machine collaboration paradigm for the subsequent Apollo, Gemini, and Space Shuttle programs. This clash not only established "human-in-the-loop" as a core principle of aerospace control, but also indirectly catalyzed the birth of "human-computer interaction" as an independent discipline in the late 1960s.
timeline.card_summary_en: Mercury astronauts fought automatic control, framing a question still open: who obeys whom?
timeline.why_it_matters_en: The dispute defined the still-unsolved question of whether the machine listens to the human or the human to the machine. From the Apollo 13 rescue in 1970 through Uber's fatal self-driving crash in 2018 to the Boeing 737 MAX in 2019, the boundary of human-in-the-loop keeps being redrawn. The AI-era copilot concept, LLM writes code while humans review, is the latest continuation of this argument.
timeline.behind_scenes_en: Of the Mercury Seven astronauts, John Glenn and Alan Shepard were the staunchest advocates of manual control. They pressured NASA through the Air Force test-pilot network until NASA compromised and added backup manual controllers to the Mercury capsule. On Glenn's 1962 first orbital flight, the capsule's attitude sensors malfunctioned and he switched to manual mode to complete the flight, proving astronaut judgment irreplaceable. That experience directly cemented the human-in-the-loop principle in Apollo's design.

timeline.title_zh: Slagle SAINT:第一个专家系统,机器解微积分
timeline.title_en: SAINT: Symbolic Automatic INTegrator
timeline.summary_zh:
1961 年 5 月 13 日,James Slagle 在 MIT 提交博士论文《A Heuristic Program that Solves Symbolic Integration Problems in Freshman Calculus, Symbolic Automatic Integrator (SAINT)》,导师 Marvin Minsky。
SAINT 用 LISP 在 IBM 7090 上实现,采用启发式搜索 + 标准 26 种积分形式 + 18 类变换,像大一学生一样按“试一下→不行再换方法”的方式求解不定积分。
在 54 道 MIT 大一微积分期末考题中,SAINT 解出 52 道(96%),平均每题两分钟。
1963 年 CACM 发表 shortened 版本后被广泛引用。
timeline.source_name: Slagle, J. R. (1961). PhD thesis, MIT; (1963) CACM 6(10):551-558
timeline.card_summary_zh: SAINT 能自动完成大学水平的符号积分题，第一次展示机器如何把数学启发式规则转化为可执行的解题过程。
timeline.summary_en: On May 13, 1961, James Slagle submitted his MIT doctoral thesis, advised by Marvin Minsky, titled "A Heuristic Program that Solves Symbolic Integration Problems in Freshman Calculus, Symbolic Automatic Integrator (SAINT)." Implemented in LISP on an IBM 7090, SAINT solved indefinite integrals like a college freshman using a "try it, and if it fails, try another method" approach, combining heuristic search with 26 standard integration forms and 18 transformations. The program successfully solved 52 of 54 MIT freshman calculus final exam questions (96%) in an average of two minutes per problem, and a shortened version published in CACM in 1963 became widely cited.
timeline.card_summary_en: SAINT solved college-level integrals automatically, turning heuristics into executable steps.
timeline.why_it_matters_en: SAINT could automatically solve university-level symbolic integration problems, first demonstrating how a machine turns mathematical heuristic rules into executable problem-solving. It ranks among the earliest domain-plus-specialized-knowledge-plus-heuristic-search programs and a prototype expert system four years before DENDRAL, to which the title of first expert system is conventionally reserved. More importantly it first proved a machine could approach human undergraduate level in one body of knowledge, turning what AI can do from abstract speculation into measurable concrete tasks.
timeline.behind_scenes_en: Slagle was a blind scholar; in 1959 President Eisenhower personally awarded him a 500-dollar scholarship for recorded materials for the blind. He completed SAINT while working at MIT Lincoln Laboratory, drafting the paper in May 1961 and publishing the expanded version in CACM 6(10):551-558 in 1963, included in Feigenbaum and Feldman's 1963 anthology Computers and Thought, which became the bible of 1960s AI researchers. Minsky recalled in The Emotion Machine that Slagle's program was almost as good as MIT's strong undergraduates, at a time when even the general theory of integration was incomplete.

timeline.title_zh: Bobrow STUDENT:英文应用题自动求解
timeline.title_en: STUDENT: Natural Language Input for a Computer Problem Solving System
timeline.summary_zh:
1964 年,Daniel Bobrow 在 MIT 完成博士论文《Natural Language Input for a Computer Problem Solving System》(MIT AI Group Technical Report TR-1),并于同年发表在 CACM 7(8):486-492(卷期号与页码待核实)。
STUDENT 把高中代数应用题(英文)解析成方程,再调用 SOLVE 模块求解,失败时通过 REMEMBER 模块补充常识(如“距离等于速度乘时间”),或向用户反问澄清。
Bobrow 把它定义为“受限领域自然语言理解”——和当时的机器翻译思路相反,STUDENT 不追求通用语法,而是在小世界里把语义和推理绑死。
timeline.source_name: Bobrow, D. G. (1964). CACM 7(8):486-492(卷期号与页码待核实); PhD thesis, MIT (TR-1)
timeline.card_summary_zh: Bobrow STUDENT：英文应用题自动求解，并成为这一阶段值得追踪的关键变化。
timeline.summary_en: In 1964, Daniel Bobrow completed his MIT PhD thesis, "Natural Language Input for a Computer Problem Solving System" (MIT AI Group Technical Report TR-1), published that same year in CACM 7(8):486-492 (volume, issue, and page numbers to be verified). His program, STUDENT, parsed English high school algebra word problems into equations and called a SOLVE module to resolve them, utilizing a REMEMBER module to supply common-sense knowledge (such as "distance equals speed times time") or asking the user clarifying questions upon failure. Bobrow defined this as "restricted-domain natural language understanding"—contrasting with the machine translation trends of the era, STUDENT did not pursue a universal grammar, opting instead to tightly bind semantics and reasoning within a small world.
timeline.card_summary_en: Bobrow's STUDENT parsed English word problems and solved them, an early illusion of understanding.
timeline.why_it_matters_en: Together with SAINT and SHRDLU, STUDENT defined the microworld route of 1960s AI, squeezing the appearance of understanding from restricted scenes and widening slowly. It was the first time a machine seemed to read a passage of English and compute an answer, a feat that remains a classic evaluation of LLM reasoning in the GPT era, with datasets like GSM8K its distant relatives.
timeline.behind_scenes_en: Bobrow's thesis was technical report number one of the MIT AI Group, supervised by Marvin Minsky. He later served as deputy director of Xerox PARC's CSL, driving the 1970s paradigm shift in natural language understanding alongside Terry Winograd and Gary Hendrix. STUDENT was reported by The New York Times as an MIT computer solving high-school algebra problems, igniting the public's first wave of AI imagination, a wave knocked back to earth after the 1973 Lighthill Report and into the first AI winter.

timeline.title_zh: McCarthy vs Engelbart:AI 与 IA 路线分道
timeline.title_en: McCarthy vs Engelbart — AI and IA Diverge
timeline.summary_zh:
1964 年前后,John McCarthy 和 Douglas Engelbart 分处两地（McCarthy 在斯坦福大学 Stanford University，Engelbart 在隔壁的 SRI 即 Stanford Research Institute，与大学是两个机构）,对“计算机该做什么”产生根本分歧。
McCarthy 主张“让机器变聪明”——AI(Artificial Intelligence),机器应自主完成更多任务。
Engelbart 主张“让人变聪明”——IA(Intelligence Augmentation),机器是放大人类智力的工具。
1968 年 Engelbart 在 FJCC（Fall Joint Computer Conference）做“Mother of All Demos”,展示鼠标、超文本、视频会议——这是 IA 路线的奠基演示。
McCarthy 则在 Stanford 创立 AI Lab(1963-1968),把 AI 推向 Lisp、知识表示、自动推理方向。
timeline.source_name: Engelbart (1962) Augmenting Human Intellect; McCarthy (1963) Stanford AI Project founding
timeline.card_summary_zh: McCarthy vs Engelbart：AI 与 IA 路线分道。
timeline.summary_en: Around 1964, John McCarthy and Douglas Engelbart were working at separate locations—McCarthy at Stanford University, and Engelbart at the neighboring SRI (Stanford Research Institute, a separate institution)—when they developed a fundamental disagreement over "what computers should do." McCarthy championed "making machines smart"—AI (Artificial Intelligence), where machines autonomously complete more tasks—while Engelbart advocated "making humans smart"—IA (Intelligence Augmentation), viewing machines as tools to amplify human intelligence. In 1968, Engelbart delivered the "Mother of All Demos" at the FJCC (Fall Joint Computer Conference), showcasing the mouse, hypertext, and video conferencing in a founding demonstration of the IA path, while McCarthy founded the Stanford AI Lab (1963-1968), pushing AI toward Lisp, knowledge representation, and automated reasoning.
timeline.card_summary_en: AI and IA split paths, autonomy versus augmentation, a fork still dividing the field today.
timeline.why_it_matters_en: Today's dispute between autonomous AGI and human-machine copilot collaboration is the continuation of McCarthy versus Engelbart. OpenAI's 2024 friction between Sam Altman and Ilya Sutskever, Anthropic's stance that Claude is an assistant not a replacement, and Apple Intelligence's augment-not-replace pitch are all contemporary projections of a line drawn sixty years ago.
timeline.behind_scenes_en: Engelbart was proposing augmentation at SRI in the 1950s while McCarthy planned the AI discipline at Dartmouth. After brief early cooperation they parted ways: McCarthy moved from MIT to Stanford in 1962 and co-founded the Stanford AI Project with Minsky in 1963, and Engelbart founded SRI's Augmentation Research Center in 1963. Their laboratories sat less than ten miles apart, yet their ideas diverged so far that they barely cited each other. Only with the spread of personal computers in the late 1980s did the IA route win vindication in GUIs, hyperlinks, and wikis.

timeline.title_zh: RAND Tablet:低成本手写图形输入设备
timeline.title_en: RAND Tablet: Low-Cost Handwriting & Graphics Input
timeline.summary_zh:
1964 年,RAND 公司发布 RAND Tablet——一台造价约 18,000 美元的电子手写板,用网格状导线感应笔尖位置,分辨率 100 dpi,刷新率 100 次/秒。
相比同期 Lincoln Labs 的 Tablet，它造价相对低，第一次让普通实验室也能上手做笔输入实验。
MCI、SRI、RAND 的研究者用它做了大量手写识别、图形界面、签名验证研究。
timeline.source_name: Davis, M. R. & Ellis, T. O. (1964). RAND Tablet: A Man-Machine Graphical Communication Device. FJCC.
timeline.card_summary_zh: RAND Tablet：低成本手写图形输入设备；RAND Tablet 是后来 Apple Newton、Palm Pilot。
timeline.summary_en: In 1964, the RAND Corporation released the RAND Tablet, an electronic writing tablet costing about $18,000 that used a grid of wires to sense the stylus tip at a resolution of 100 dpi and a refresh rate of 100 times per second. Relatively cheaper than Lincoln Labs' contemporary tablet, it allowed ordinary labs to run pen-input experiments for the first time. Researchers at MCI, SRI, and RAND used it to conduct extensive studies on handwriting recognition, graphical interfaces, and signature verification.
timeline.card_summary_en: A low-cost pen-input tablet, ancestor of the Newton, Palm Pilot, Wacom, and iPad plus Pencil.
timeline.why_it_matters_en: The RAND Tablet is the ancestor of the whole pen-input plus recognition line running through Apple Newton, Palm Pilot, Wacom tablets, and iPad with Pencil. It turned writing on paper into a stream of signals a computer could capture for the first time, and online handwriting recognition stood up as a discipline branch from then on.
timeline.behind_scenes_en: The tablet was designed principally by M. R. Davis and T. O. Ellis, with the paper presented at the 1964 Fall Joint Computer Conference. Together with Engelbart's contemporaneous NLS mouse and Sutherland's Sketchpad of 1963, it formed the hardware foundation of human-computer interaction emerging as an independent direction in the 1960s. Yet mature pen input had to wait for the failure of Apple's Newton and the success of Palm in the 1990s, with three intervening decades dominated by mice and keyboards.

timeline.title_zh: DENDRAL 启动:第一个大型知识驱动专家系统
timeline.title_en: DENDRAL Project: First Knowledge-Intensive Expert System
timeline.summary_zh:
1965 年春,Edward Feigenbaum 刚加入 Stanford 任计算机系创始教员,立刻与诺奖遗传学家 Joshua Lederberg 启动 DENDRAL 项目,目标是让计算机从有机化合物的质谱图反推分子结构。
1966 年 Lederberg 拉入 Carl Djerassi(口服避孕药之父、Stanford 质谱实验室负责人)补齐化学知识。
项目持续到 1982,是史上第一个大型“知识库 + 推理机”专家系统。
核心思想——“程序的能力来自具体领域知识,而不是更聪明的推理”——被称为“知识原理”,1980 年代专家系统工业化的理论基石。
timeline.source_name: Lindsay, Buchanan, Feigenbaum, Lederberg (1993). DENDRAL: A case study. AI Journal 61:209-261.
timeline.card_summary_zh: DENDRAL 把化学家的经验写成可推理的规则，第一次证明 AI 能在狭窄但真实的专业领域超过普通人。
timeline.summary_en: In the spring of 1965, freshly appointed Stanford computer science founding faculty member Edward Feigenbaum partnered with Nobel laureate geneticist Joshua Lederberg to launch the DENDRAL project, aiming to make computers deduce molecular structures from the mass spectra of organic compounds. In 1966, Lederberg recruited Carl Djerassi—the father of the oral contraceptive pill and head of Stanford's mass spectrometry lab—to provide the crucial chemistry expertise. Running until 1982 as history's first large-scale "knowledge base + inference engine" expert system, its core philosophy that a program's power derives from domain-specific knowledge rather than smarter reasoning was dubbed the "knowledge principle," serving as the theoretical cornerstone for the industrialization of expert systems in the 1980s.
timeline.card_summary_en: It wrote chemists' expertise into rules, proving AI could beat novices in a narrow real domain.
timeline.why_it_matters_en: DENDRAL pulled AI from the dream of a universal reasoner down to the reality that domain knowledge is the key, directly spawning MYCIN, XCON, PROSPECTOR, and a generation of 1970s-80s expert systems. Feigenbaum became known as the father of expert systems and received the 1994 ACM Turing Award. Knowledge engineering as a profession began with DENDRAL, and today's prompt engineer is its distant descendant.
timeline.behind_scenes_en: The original design inspiration came from Lederberg's 1964 DENDRAL algorithm, a generator exhaustively enumerating all possible molecular structures. Exhaustion produces astronomical candidate structures, so chemists' heuristics had to prune them. Feigenbaum's key insight was to encode the chemists' experience directly into the program instead of simulating how scientists think. That trade of knowledge versus reasoning shaped the next twenty years of AI routes, and planted the seed of the expert-system bubble bursting in the late 1980s, since the knowledge-acquisition bottleneck remains unsolved.

timeline.title_zh: Ivakhnenko GMDH:第一个深度学习算法
timeline.title_en: Ivakhnenko's Group Method of Data Handling (GMDH)
timeline.summary_zh:
1965 年,乌克兰控制论学者 Alexey Ivakhnenko 与 Valentin Lapa 发表《Cybernetics and Forecasting Techniques》,提出 GMDH(Group Method of Data Handling,数据群处理法)——第一个能端到端训练深度前馈多层感知机的通用学习算法。
GMDH 用回归分析逐层增长网络,每层用单独验证集做剪枝,1971 年 Ivakhnenko 已实现 8 层深度网络——比西方“深度学习”概念早 30 多年。
timeline.source_name: Ivakhnenko, A. G. & Lapa, V. G. (1965). Cybernetics and Forecasting Techniques. Kiev: Naukova Dumka.
timeline.card_summary_zh: Ivakhnenko GMDH：第一个深度学习算法；GMDH 是“深度学习”真正的起点。
timeline.summary_en: In 1965, Ukrainian cyberneticians Alexey Ivakhnenko and Valentin Lapa published *Cybernetics and Forecasting Techniques*, introducing GMDH (Group Method of Data Handling)—the first general learning algorithm capable of training deep feedforward multilayer perceptrons end-to-end. By using regression analysis to grow the network layer by layer and pruning each layer with a separate validation set, Ivakhnenko had already implemented an 8-layer deep network by 1971, predating the Western concept of "deep learning" by more than 30 years.
timeline.card_summary_en: Ivakhnenko's GMDH is deep learning's true starting point, decades early and half a world away.
timeline.why_it_matters_en: GMDH is the real starting point of deep learning, and Schmidhuber accordingly calls Ivakhnenko the father of deep learning. Four years ahead of Minsky and Papert's pessimistic single-layer verdict in their 1969 Perceptrons, it proved that stacking layers to learn internal representations was already a walked path in the Soviet Union. Today's three essentials of deep learning, stacked layers, validation-set pruning, and internal representation learning, were all present in GMDH.
timeline.behind_scenes_en: Ivakhnenko worked at the Institute of Cybernetics of the Academy of Sciences of Ukraine in Kyiv and formally established the GMDH algorithmic system in 1968. Cold War language barriers confined his work to the Soviet Union and Eastern Europe until Japanese scholars introduced it to the West in 1971, and Farlow's 1980s English anthology brought wide recognition. After the Soviet collapse in 1989, GMDH was rediscovered in economic forecasting and ecological modeling. When the 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics went to Hinton and Hopfield, Schmidhuber publicly protested, calling it a Nobel prize for copying, and named Ivakhnenko in 1965, Amari in 1967, and Linnainmaa in 1970 as overlooked pioneers.

timeline.title_zh: Weizenbaum ELIZA:第一个聊天机器人的诞生
timeline.title_en: ELIZA: A Computer Program for the Study of Natural Language Communication
timeline.summary_zh:
1965 年,Joseph Weizenbaum 在 MIT Project MAC 用 MAD-SLIP 在 IBM 7094 上写出 ELIZA,通过 CTSS 分时系统让多个用户同时与程序对话。
ELIZA 是一个平台:换不同“脚本”就变不同角色。
最有名的脚本是 DOCTOR——模仿 Rogerian 心理治疗师,用“你刚才说...”“这让你想到什么?”等反问模板把用户的话包装成回应。
1966 年 1 月 CACM 9(1):36-45 发表,ELIZA 立刻成为史上第一个被普通用户当作“懂人话”的程序。
timeline.source_name: Weizenbaum, J. (1966). CACM 9(1):36-45
timeline.card_summary_zh: ELIZA 只靠简单规则复述用户的话，却让人产生“机器理解我”的错觉，人机对话的心理效应首次显形。
timeline.summary_en: In 1965, Joseph Weizenbaum wrote ELIZA in MAD-SLIP on an IBM 7094 at MIT Project MAC, using the CTSS time-sharing system to allow multiple users to converse with the program simultaneously. Designed as a platform that could adopt different personas by swapping "scripts," its most famous was DOCTOR—which mimicked a Rogerian psychotherapist by repackaging user statements into reflective questions like "You said..." and "What does that make you think of?". Published in January 1966 in *CACM* 9(1):36-45, ELIZA instantly became the first program in history that ordinary users treated as genuinely understanding human language.
timeline.card_summary_en: Simple rules echoing users' own words made people feel understood, and the ELIZA effect was born.
timeline.why_it_matters_en: ELIZA relied on nothing but simple rules restating users' words, yet created the illusion that the machine understands me, the first surfacing of the psychology of human-machine conversation. It was the first broad experience of a machine seeming to understand you: Weizenbaum's secretary asked him to leave the room after twenty minutes, unwilling to bare her heart to the machine in front of him. The ELIZA effect of users over-identifying with machines remains central to chatbot design and the origin of concerns about anthropomorphic misdirection in evaluating GPT, Claude, and Gemini.
timeline.behind_scenes_en: Weizenbaum's intent was a platform for studying human-machine conversation, not a chatbot; the DOCTOR script was a casual demonstration that ended up stealing the show, running off, as he put it, to prove things he never intended to prove. Once the magic was discovered, Bernie Cosell rewrote a version in Lisp at BBN and it spread through ARPANET across academia, binding ELIZA to Lisp while the original MAD-SLIP version was forgotten for fifty years. Weizenbaum later wrote Computer Power and Human Reason in 1976 warning against misuse of AI, becoming one of the earliest critics of AI ethics.

timeline.title_zh: Zadeh 模糊集合:让数学承认“差不多”
timeline.title_en: Fuzzy Sets
timeline.summary_zh:
1965 年 6 月,Lotfi Zadeh 在《Information and Control》8(3):338-353 发表《Fuzzy Sets》。
文章定义了“模糊集合”——元素对集合的隶属度不再是 0 或 1,而是 0 到 1 之间的任意实数。
并给出并、交、补等基本运算。
Zadeh 的论点很直接:现实世界中“高”“年轻”“差不多热”这类概念本身就有渐变,经典集合论逼着机器用 0/1 二选一,反而丢掉了人类推理里最关键的灰度信息。
timeline.source_name: Zadeh, L. A. (1965). Information and Control 8(3):338-353
timeline.card_summary_zh: 模糊集合允许隶属度处在 0 与 1 之间，让机器第一次能够用数学方式处理“有点像”和“差不多”。
timeline.summary_en: In June 1965, Lotfi Zadeh published "Fuzzy Sets" in *Information and Control* 8(3):338-353, defining "fuzzy sets"—where an element's membership in a set is no longer a binary 0 or 1, but any real number between 0 and 1—and detailing basic operations like union, intersection, and complement. Zadeh’s argument was straightforward: real-world concepts like "tall," "young," and "about hot" are inherently gradual, and forcing machines to make a binary choice between 0 and 1 via classical set theory discards the crucial gray areas of human reasoning.
timeline.card_summary_en: Membership between 0 and 1 let mathematics finally handle kind-of and almost.
timeline.why_it_matters_en: Fuzzy sets let mathematics admit that vagueness itself can be handled precisely. They spawned fuzzy logic and fuzzy control, and in the 1980s-90s Japanese appliances, from Panasonic washers to Mitsubishi air conditioners and the Sendai subway, shipped products that could judge. Washing machines weighing loads, air conditioners holding temperature, and camera autofocus still run fuzzy controllers today. In the LLM era fuzzy sets return as soft labels, membership scores, and token probabilities.
timeline.behind_scenes_en: Zadeh was born in Azerbaijan to an Iranian family, moved to the United States in 1944, and taught for decades at UC Berkeley. When he wrote Fuzzy Sets he was already an IEEE Fellow and a control-theory authority, yet chose to challenge the roots of classical set theory, drawing nearly twenty years of cold shoulder from the Western mathematical mainstream. Japan and the Soviet Union adopted fastest: the Sendai subway has run on fuzzy control since 1987 with zero accidents, while America only followed at scale in the 1990s. Zadeh lived to 96, dying in 2017, and watched his ideas come back around in the LLM era.

timeline.title_zh: Amari 用随机梯度下降训练多层感知机
timeline.title_en: Amari's SGD for Multilayer Perceptrons
timeline.summary_zh:
1967 年,甘利俊一(Shun-ichi Amari)在日本发表用随机梯度下降(SGD)训练多层感知机的方法,并在 5 层网络(其中 2 层可修改)上做非线性可分模式分类实验。
这是已知最早的端到端梯度训练多层网络的工作——比 Western 文献中广为引用的 Werbos 1974 反向传播早 7 年,比 Rumelhart-Hinton-Williams 1986 的反向传播普及早近 20 年。
timeline.source_name: Amari, S. (1967). A theory of adaptive pattern classifiers. IEEE Trans. EC-16(3):299-307.
timeline.card_summary_zh: Amari 用随机梯度下降训练多层感知机；Amari 的工作证明“梯度下降可以训练多层网络”这件事在 1967 年就被解决过一次。
timeline.summary_en: In 1967, Shun-ichi Amari published a method in Japan for training multilayer perceptrons using stochastic gradient descent (SGD), conducting non-linearly separable pattern classification experiments on a 5-layer network (where 2 layers were modifiable). This is the earliest known work on end-to-end gradient training of multilayer networks—predating the widely cited Werbos 1974 backpropagation in Western literature by 7 years, and the popularization of backpropagation by Rumelhart-Hinton-Williams in 1986 by nearly 20 years.
timeline.card_summary_en: Amari trained multilayer perceptrons with stochastic gradient descent, solving it once in 1967.
timeline.why_it_matters_en: His work proved gradient descent can train multilayer networks, settled once back in 1967. That the Minsky-Papert pessimism misled the field for fifteen years owes partly to Amari publishing in Japanese with limited circulation. Today's core training recipe, SGD plus backpropagation, is effectively the synthesis of Amari 1967, Linnainmaa 1970, and Rumelhart 1986.
timeline.behind_scenes_en: Amari holds a mathematics doctorate from the University of Tokyo and later founded information geometry as a new discipline. His 1967 paper ran in a Japanese domestic journal, so AI history in the English-speaking world long overlooked it. Schmidhuber wrote repeatedly from 2014 to 2024 pressing priority claims for Amari and Ivakhnenko, noting that the Hopfield 1982 network essentially replicates Amari's 1972 adaptive Ising model. Amari received the Kyoto Prize in 2025, after the 2024 physics Nobel for Hopfield and Hinton sparked debate over forgotten Japanese pioneers.

timeline.title_zh: Winograd SHRDLU:积木世界里的“理解”
timeline.title_en: SHRDLU: Understanding Natural Language in a Blocks World
timeline.summary_zh:
1968-1970 年,Terry Winograd 在 MIT 开发 SHRDLU,作为博士论文(1970 完成;论文 1971 年以 MIT AI-TR-235 正式发表)。
程序运行在 DEC PDP-6 上,用 Micro Planner + Lisp 写成,用户通过电传打字机与一个虚拟“积木世界”对话——指令 SHRDLU 把红色方块放到绿色立方体上,问“刚才你拿起的是哪个?”,SHRDLU 会回答、追问、纠正、推理。
1972 年论文以《Understanding Natural Language》出书(Academic Press),被认为是 1970 年代自然语言理解的最高成就。
timeline.source_name: Winograd, T. (1972). Understanding Natural Language. Academic Press. PhD thesis, MIT, 1970.
timeline.card_summary_zh: SHRDLU 能听懂指令、追踪上下文并操作虚拟积木，却也暴露了 AI 一离开封闭世界就会失灵的边界。
timeline.summary_en: Between 1968 and 1970, Terry Winograd developed SHRDLU at MIT for his PhD thesis, which was completed in 1970 and officially published in 1971 as MIT AI-TR-235. Running on a DEC PDP-6 and written in Micro Planner and Lisp, the program allowed users to converse with a virtual "blocks world" via teletype—instructing SHRDLU to put a red block on a green cube or asking "which one did you just pick up?" as the system answered, asked follow-up questions, corrected, and reasoned. In 1972, the thesis was published as a book, *Understanding Natural Language* (Academic Press), and went on to be recognized as the crowning achievement of 1970s natural language understanding.
timeline.card_summary_en: SHRDLU took instructions, tracked context, and moved blocks, exposing AI's closed-world limits.
timeline.why_it_matters_en: For the first time a program looked like it genuinely understood language, combining syntax, semantics, reasoning, memory, and planning into a visible engineering system. Later NLP researchers either patched SHRDLU's path or, like Winograd himself, turned against it: by the late 1970s at Stanford he shifted to HCI and Heidegger, arguing the route fails because it depends on a closed world, a reflection that steered NLP through the 1980s-90s.
timeline.behind_scenes_en: Winograd was then 24, supervised by Marvin Minsky. The name comes from ETAOIN SHRDLU, the second row of Linotype keys ordered by letter frequency, the garbled placeholder of old typesetting errors. SHRDLU looked like a general dialogue system but worked only inside a fifty-word blocks world, the peak and endpoint of the 1960s microworld route. Winograd later reflected that we assumed enlarging the blocks world gave the real one, but the real world has no clean boundaries and no perfectly aligned semantics, a line quoted again and again in the LLM era: is GPT-4 just a bigger SHRDLU that seems to understand?

timeline.title_zh: Knuth《The Art of Computer Programming》Vol.1 出版
timeline.title_en: Knuth: The Art of Computer Programming, Vol. 1 (1968)
timeline.summary_zh:
1968 年,Donald Knuth 出版《The Art of Computer Programming》第一卷《Fundamental Algorithms》。
Knuth 计划写 7 卷,到 2024 年只出了 1-4A 卷,但已完成的卷被誉为“算法圣经”,是计算机科学作为独立学科的奠基文献之一。
Knuth 同时启动 TeX 排版项目(1977),其结果 TeX/LaTeX 成为之后 50 年所有科学论文的标准排版工具。
timeline.source_name: Knuth, D. E. (1968). The Art of Computer Programming, Vol. 1. Addison-Wesley.
timeline.card_summary_zh: Knuth《The Art of Computer Programming》Vol.1 出版。
timeline.summary_en: In 1968, Donald Knuth published *Fundamental Algorithms*, the first volume of *The Art of Computer Programming*. Although Knuth planned for seven volumes, only Volumes 1-4A have been released as of 2024, yet the completed work is hailed as the "bible of algorithms" and stands as a founding text of computer science as an independent discipline. Knuth also launched the TeX typesetting project (1977), resulting in TeX/LaTeX, which became the standard typesetting tool for all scientific papers over the next 50 years.
timeline.card_summary_en: TAOCP lifted algorithms from engineering practice into provable, analyzable mathematical objects.
timeline.why_it_matters_en: It raised algorithms into mathematical objects you can prove things about, the methodological source of all algorithm-complexity analysis, model-efficiency work, and FLOPS accounting in the AI era. Knuth's literate programming idea lives on in the code-plus-narrative style of Jupyter notebooks and Observable, and premature optimization is the root of all evil remains engineering's most quoted maxim.
timeline.behind_scenes_en: In 1962, still a Caltech graduate student, Knuth was approached by an Addison-Wesley editor to write a small compiler book. It kept growing; volume one passed 600 pages by publication in 1968. Knuth himself estimated completion needed another twenty years, and sixty years on it remains unfinished. He long ran Computer Musings lectures at Stanford, saying publicly in 2014 that he had given up finishing all seven volumes in his lifetime but would bring each to a state worth finishing. He stayed close to AI academia, his doctoral students including Vaughan Pratt, though Robert Tarjan's formal advisor was Robert Floyd with Knuth only one of his academic advisors.

timeline.title_zh: Engelbart「演示之母」:NLS 与个人计算诞生
timeline.title_en: The Mother of All Demos (Engelbart, 1968-12-09)
timeline.summary_zh:
1968 年 12 月 9 日,Douglas Engelbart 在旧金山 Fall Joint Computer Conference 上做了 90 分钟演示,首次公开展示 NLS(oN-Line System):鼠标、超文本链接、实时文字编辑、屏幕窗口、视频会议、协作文档、版本控制——今天个人计算的所有核心要素。
Engelbart 远程连线 SRI 实验室,让团队现场协作编辑一份结构化文档。
演示被称作“The Mother of All Demos”——之后的 Apple Macintosh 发布(1984)、iPhone 发布(2007)都被视作它的延续。
timeline.source_name: Engelbart, D. (1968). A Research Center for Augmenting Human Intellect. FJCC.
timeline.card_summary_zh: Engelbart「演示之母」：NLS 与个人计算诞生；次演示定义了“人机交互”作为独立学科的边界。
timeline.summary_en: On December 9, 1968, Douglas Engelbart delivered a 90-minute presentation at the Fall Joint Computer Conference in San Francisco, publicly debuting NLS (oN-Line System) to showcase the mouse, hypertext links, real-time text editing, screen windows, video conferencing, collaborative documents, and version control—all the core elements of modern personal computing. Connecting remotely to the SRI lab to collaboratively edit a structured document live with his team, Engelbart pulled off what became legendary as "The Mother of All Demos," a landmark event whose lineage continues through the subsequent launches of the Apple Macintosh (1984) and the iPhone (2007).
timeline.card_summary_en: Engelbart's 1968 demo drew the boundary lines of human-computer interaction as its own field.
timeline.why_it_matters_en: That single demo fixed HCI as an independent discipline. Mouse, hyperlinks, and collaborative editing were commercialized by Apple, Microsoft, and Tim Berners-Lee in the 1980s-90s and became the basis of every desktop and mobile device today. Engelbart's augmentation route, IA, is mainstream again in the LLM era: Notion AI, Cursor, and Copilot all extend his 1968 vision.
timeline.behind_scenes_en: Reading Vannevar Bush's As We May Think in the 1950s, Engelbart resolved to build memex. In 1962 he published Augmenting Human Intellect: A Conceptual Framework and won ARPA funding for SRI's Augmentation Research Center. The 1968 demo connected back to SRI over dedicated links, microwave video plus audio return, and an audience above a thousand watched a link clicked with a mouse without grasping they were seeing the embryo of the next fifty years of computing. Engelbart felt lifelong that Silicon Valley took his ideas without credit; even Apple's 1979 PARC visit to study the Alto drew on NLS thinking.

timeline.title_zh: Minsky-Papert《Perceptrons》:神经网络第一次大挫折
timeline.title_en: Perceptrons (Minsky & Papert, MIT Press, 1969)
timeline.summary_zh:
1969 年,Marvin Minsky 和 Seymour Papert 出版《Perceptrons: An Introduction to Computational Geometry》(MIT Press)。
书中用严格数学证明:单层感知机无法表达 XOR、连通性等基本函数,要表达这些函数必须靠多层网络,而多层网络当时没有可用的训练算法。
1988 年扩展版(含 Epilogue)承认原版部分论断被过度外推——但 1969 年原版引发的“神经网络死路”印象已经形成,直接促成 1970 年代第一次 AI 寒冬。
timeline.source_name: Minsky, M. & Papert, S. (1969). Perceptrons. MIT Press.
timeline.card_summary_zh: Minsky-Papert《Perceptrons》：神经网络第一次大挫折；是 AI 史上被引用最多、误读最多的一本书。
timeline.summary_en: In 1969, Marvin Minsky and Seymour Papert published *Perceptrons: An Introduction to Computational Geometry* (MIT Press), proving mathematically that single-layer perceptrons could not represent basic functions like XOR or connectivity, which required multi-layer networks that lacked viable training algorithms at the time. While their 1988 expanded edition (including an Epilogue) admitted that some of these claims had been over-extrapolated, the original book had already cemented the impression that neural networks were a dead end, directly triggering the first AI winter of the 1970s.
timeline.card_summary_en: AI's most cited and most misread book brought neural networks their first great setback.
timeline.why_it_matters_en: The book discussed only single-layer perceptrons but was read as all neural networks fail, drying up research money through the 1970s-80s and driving researchers out of the field. When Rosenblatt died in a 1971 boating accident, nobody carried on his multilayer work. Only the 1986 Rumelhart-Hinton-Williams backpropagation paper broke the misreading, and on winning the Nobel in 2024 Hinton still spoke of this book's hold on him.
timeline.behind_scenes_en: While Minsky and Papert wrote it, Rosenblatt was their colleague and friend. The text never declares neural networks dead, but the last chapter of the 1969 first edition leaned hard on constructions like the perceptron will not, and MIT Press marketing cemented the public sense that AI academia had pronounced them finished. Papert later admitted they meant to write a rigorous book and produced a bomb instead. Rosenblatt never got to defend himself, lost in a boating accident on his 43rd birthday in July 1971, and American neural-network funding reportedly fell some ninety percent in the five years after his death, ratio pending verification.

timeline.title_zh: SRI Shakey:第一个会推理的移动机器人
timeline.title_en: Shakey: First Mobile Robot with Reasoning
timeline.summary_zh:
1966-1972 年,SRI International(Charles Rosen + Nils Nilsson 团队)开发 Shakey——第一个能感知环境、规划路径、执行动作的自主移动机器人。
1969 年第一版完成:装电视摄像头、激光测距仪、碰撞传感器,通过无线连到 DEC PDP-10/PDP-15 上跑规划与感知。
1971-1972 年 Fikes+Nilsson 发表 STRIPS 规划器,把“动作 = 前提条件 + 删除表 + 添加表”形式化,成为之后 30 年机器人规划的事实标准。
timeline.source_name: Nilsson, N. J. (1984). Shakey the Robot. SRI AI Center Technical Note 323.
timeline.card_summary_zh: Shakey 把感知、规划和行动装进同一台移动机器人，第一次让机器根据环境自主决定下一步。
timeline.summary_en: From 1966 to 1972, SRI International (led by Charles Rosen and Nils Nilsson) developed Shakey, the first autonomous mobile robot capable of perceiving its environment, planning paths, and executing actions. Completed in 1969, the first version carried a TV camera, a laser rangefinder, and bump sensors, wirelessly connecting to a DEC PDP-10/PDP-15 to run its planning and perception. In 1971-1972, Fikes and Nilsson published the STRIPS planner, formalizing "action = preconditions + delete list + add list" into the de facto standard for robot planning for the next 30 years.
timeline.card_summary_en: Shakey packed perception, planning, and action into one mobile robot choosing its own next move.
timeline.why_it_matters_en: Shakey contributed A* search, the Hough transform, visibility graphs, STRIPS, and layered architecture at once, the algorithmic bedrock of every mobile robot since, from vacuum cleaners and self-driving cars to Mars rovers and warehouse robots. Inducted into Carnegie Mellon's Robot Hall of Fame in 2004, its line lives on in OpenAI-era robot research and Waymo path planning through STRIPS variants.
timeline.behind_scenes_en: The name came from its wobbly gait, the rooftop camera so heavy the robot often paused mid-move. Charles Rosen proposed the project in 1963, the proposal went to DARPA in 1965 securing 750,000 dollars, about 5.8 million today, figure pending verification, and launch followed in 1966. At the first complete demonstration in 1969 Shakey independently found an object in a room and pushed it aside, and Life magazine called it the first electronic person. Nilsson later recalled expecting household robots within ten years, a road still unfinished after fifty.

timeline.title_zh: Minsky 获 ACM Turing Award:AI 第一次拿“计算机诺贝尔”
timeline.title_en: Marvin Minsky Receives ACM Turing Award
timeline.summary_zh:
1969 年,ACM 将图灵奖颁给 Marvin Minsky,表彰他在《Computation: Finite and Infinite Machines》(1967)、《Semantic Information Processing》(1968) 等著作中对计算理论、AI、认知科学的综合贡献。
Minsky 是 AI 领域第一位图灵奖得主,比 Dijkstra(1972)、McCarthy(1971)、Newell-Simon(1975)都早。
timeline.source_name: ACM Turing Award citation, Marvin Minsky, 1969
timeline.card_summary_zh: Minsky 成为首位获得图灵奖的 AI 研究者，人工智能由此正式进入计算机科学最高荣誉的核心视野。
timeline.summary_en: In 1969, the ACM awarded the Turing Award to Marvin Minsky, recognizing his comprehensive contributions to computation theory, AI, and cognitive science in works such as *Computation: Finite and Infinite Machines* (1967) and *Semantic Information Processing* (1968). Minsky was the first Turing Award winner in the field of AI, preceding Dijkstra (1972), McCarthy (1971), and Newell-Simon (1975).
timeline.card_summary_en: Minsky became the first AI researcher to take the Turing Award, AI entering computing's honors.
timeline.why_it_matters_en: The award itself marked AI's formal recognition by mainstream computer science at the end of the 1960s. McCarthy in 1971, Newell and Simon in 1975, Feigenbaum in 1994, Pearl in 2011, and Hinton, LeCun, and Bengio in 2018 followed, steadily consolidating the discipline's standing. Minsky's Turing lecture Form and Content in Computer Science became a classic, insisting programs must be comprehensible to people and not merely correct.
timeline.behind_scenes_en: Born in New York in 1927, Minsky took his mathematics doctorate at Princeton and built SNARC in 1951, the first neural-network learning machine, with 40 neurons and adjustable weights. He joined MIT in 1958 and co-founded the AI Project with McCarthy. Practically single-handed he trained a roster of leading scholars, Terry Winograd, Patrick Winston, Gerald Sussman, and collaborator Seymour Papert, who carried AI through the 1970s-80s. He died in 2016, only two years before Hinton and company took the 2018 award, missing the LLM-era eruption built on foundations he laid in 1969.

timeline.title_zh: IJCAI-1 第一届国际人工智能联合会议
timeline.title_en: First International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI-1)
timeline.summary_zh:
1969 年 5 月 7-9 日,第一届 IJCAI 在华盛顿举行,由 Allen Newell、Marvin Minsky、John McCarthy、Arthur Samuel 等发起,60 多位研究者参加。
会议确立了 AI 作为独立学科的学术共同体身份,首次把分散在 IEEE、ACM、心理学、控制论等领域的 AI 研究者聚到一起。
之后 IJCAI 变成两年一次的旗舰会议,1979 年 AAAI 成立后与之并行。
timeline.source_name: IJCAI-1 Proceedings (1969). Washington, D.C., May 7-9.
timeline.card_summary_zh: 首届 IJCAI 把分散在计算机、心理学与控制论中的研究者聚到一起，AI 从研究方向成长为国际学术共同体。
timeline.summary_en: From May 7–9, 1969, the inaugural IJCAI was held in Washington, initiated by Allen Newell, Marvin Minsky, John McCarthy, Arthur Samuel, and others, with over 60 researchers in attendance. The event established AI’s identity as an independent academic discipline, bringing together researchers previously scattered across IEEE, ACM, psychology, cybernetics, and other fields. IJCAI subsequently became a biennial flagship conference, running in parallel with AAAI after its founding in 1979.
timeline.card_summary_en: The first IJCAI united researchers across computing, psychology, and cybernetics as one community.
timeline.why_it_matters_en: IJCAI is where AI's institutional life began. Before it, AI papers scattered across whatever conference would take them; after it, AI had a home field. When the 1973 Lighthill Report slashed British funding, the IJCAI community was among the few forces able to answer collectively. NeurIPS, ICML, and ICLR today all trace their model back to IJCAI-1.
timeline.behind_scenes_en: The proceedings ran only 643 pages, page count pending verification, with some sixty attendees, against IJCAI 2023's 5,000-plus papers and 10,000-plus participants, a measure of how small the circle still was in 1969. Main topics were theorem proving, vision, planning, natural language, and knowledge representation, still AI's core agenda sixty years later with Lisp swapped for PyTorch. Marvin Minsky's opening address predicted AI would settle most intellectual problems within twenty years, an optimism that became an ironic footnote of the coming winters.

timeline.title_zh: Linnainmaa 反向模式自动微分
timeline.title_en: Linnainmaa's Reverse-Mode Automatic Differentiation
timeline.summary_zh:
1970 年,芬兰数学家 Seppo Linnainmaa 在赫尔辛基大学硕士论文《The representation of the cumulative rounding error of an algorithm as a Taylor expansion of the local rounding errors》中首次给出反向模式自动微分的完整算法描述,把链式法则从输出端往输入端递归展开,把任意复合函数的偏导数压缩到一次正向 + 一次反向扫描。
这就是后来深度学习训练里“反向传播”的数学本体。
论文本身用 Fortran 做浮点舍入误差分析,只字未提神经网络。
timeline.source_name: Linnainmaa, S. (1970). M.Sc. thesis, University of Helsinki; (1976) BIT 16(2):146-160
timeline.card_summary_zh: Linnainmaa 反向模式自动微分；反向模式 AD 是整个深度学习的底层齿轮。
timeline.summary_en: In 1970, Finnish mathematician Seppo Linnainmaa first described the complete algorithm for reverse-mode automatic differentiation in his University of Helsinki master’s thesis, *The representation of the cumulative rounding error of an algorithm as a Taylor expansion of the local rounding errors*, recursively expanding the chain rule from output to input to compress the partial derivatives of any composite function into a single forward and backward pass. This became the mathematical essence of "backpropagation" in deep learning training. Yet, the thesis itself used Fortran to analyze floating-point rounding errors and never once mentioned neural networks.
timeline.card_summary_en: Reverse-mode automatic differentiation is the low-level gear underneath all of deep learning.
timeline.why_it_matters_en: Every training run behind GPT, Stable Diffusion, and AlphaFold rests on this scan: evaluate forward once, then compute every partial derivative backward in a single pass. Grasping the 1970 line makes clear how mathematics often arrives decades before machines and compute catch up.
timeline.behind_scenes_en: Linnainmaa wrote the paper as neural networks touched bottom. Minsky and Papert's Perceptrons had just come out in 1969 and connectionism was broadly written off. Working in that climate, he framed reverse-mode AD purely as a numerical computing tool, unaware it unlocked precisely the deadlock of untrainable multilayer perceptrons. Schmidhuber and others excavated the paper twenty-four years later, and the field discovered backpropagation's mathematics had been lying in Finland for over two decades.

timeline.title_zh: SHRDLU:最早的自然语言理解程序
timeline.title_en: SHRDLU: Natural Language Understanding in a Blocks World
timeline.summary_zh:
1968-1970 年,Terry Winograd 在 MIT 完成博士论文《Procedures as a Representation for Datain a Computer Program for Understanding Natural Language》,1970 年初答辩,1971 年作为 MIT AI TR-235 正式发表。
SHRDLU 让用户用普通英语指挥一个虚拟“积木世界”里的机械臂:“把那个红色方块放到蓝色立方体上”,“刚才你碰过那个金字塔吗”。
程序能理解指代、时态、上下文、规划与回指,并能解释自己的操作理由。
在 1970 年的算力下,它在封闭世界里达成了惊人的语言理解水平。
timeline.source_name: Winograd, T. (1971). MIT AI TR-235; (1972) Cognitive Psychology 3(1):1-191
timeline.card_summary_zh: SHRDLU 能在积木世界中理解指令与上下文，既代表符号语言理解的高峰，也暴露了封闭环境的局限。
timeline.summary_en: Between 1968 and 1970, Terry Winograd wrote his MIT doctoral thesis, "Procedures as a Representation for Data in a Computer Program for Understanding Natural Language"—defending it in early 1970 and officially publishing it in 1971 as MIT AI TR-235. His program, SHRDLU, allowed users to command a robotic arm in a virtual "blocks world" using plain English, such as "put that red block on the blue cube" or "did you touch that pyramid just now?" Despite the limited computing power of 1970, it achieved an astonishing level of language understanding within a closed world, handling reference, tense, context, planning, and anaphora, while even explaining the logic behind its actions.
timeline.card_summary_en: Inside its tiny blocks world SHRDLU tracked instructions and context, symbolic NLP's peak.
timeline.why_it_matters_en: SHRDLU is both the summit of symbolic NLP and the start of its decline. It proved a small world plus strong rules can carry language understanding, and exposed the deadlock that rules explode once the world grows. Today's LLMs attack Winograd's problem by another road, statistics plus massive data, yet the blocks-world paradigm remains a standard model for teaching and testing reasoning.
timeline.behind_scenes_en: Its success rested on three hidden limits: a world of a few dozen blocks with a short vocabulary; grammar rules and semantic networks hand-written line by line by Winograd; and a PDP-6 or PDP-10 running a LISP interpreter on very small memory. Reviewing the work in Cognitive Science in 1980, Winograd said he had underestimated how hard it would be to extend any of it to the real world. The better SHRDLU performed, the more people believed natural language would fall to writing enough rules.

timeline.title_zh: Intel 4004:首颗商用微处理器
timeline.title_en: Intel 4004: First Commercial Microprocessor
timeline.summary_zh:
1971 年 11 月 15 日,Intel 发布 4004 微处理器。
这是全球第一款商用单芯片微处理器,把一台完整中央处理器的逻辑(2300 个晶体管,740 kHz,4 位字长,10 微米工艺)压进 16 针 DIP 封装里。
Federico Faggin、Marcian Hoff、Stanley Mazor 设计,Busicom 计算器是原始客户。
Intel 以 6 万美元从 Busicom 买回 4004 的非独家授权,允许 Intel 把它当通用产品卖。
这是微处理器从“为某个客户定制”变成“通用计算元件”的转折点。
timeline.source_name: Intel 4004 datasheet (1971); Faggin, F. (2009) IEEE Annals of the History of Computing 31(2)
timeline.card_summary_zh: Intel 发布 4004 微处理器；微处理器让算力从机房走进桌面、家庭和工厂。
timeline.summary_en: On November 15, 1971, Intel released the 4004, the world's first commercial single-chip microprocessor, which packed the logic of a complete CPU (2300 transistors, 740 kHz, 4-bit word length, 10-micron process) into a 16-pin DIP package. Designed by Federico Faggin, Marcian Hoff, and Stanley Mazor with the Busicom calculator as the original customer, the project became the turning point where microprocessors transitioned from custom-made client chips to universal computing components after Intel bought back the non-exclusive rights from Busicom for $60,000 to sell it as a general-purpose product.
timeline.card_summary_en: The 4004 carried computing power out of the machine room toward desks, homes, and factories.
timeline.why_it_matters_en: Microprocessors made compute cheap and widespread. Without this hardware line there is no Altair in 1975, no Apple II in 1977, no IBM PC in 1981, and none of the soil that later let individuals train neural networks in their bedrooms.
timeline.behind_scenes_en: Before the 4004, a computer's CPU was a whole cabinet of circuit boards no small company could afford. At sixty dollars a chip, the 4004 turned computing into a retailable component. Faggin later left Intel to found Zilog and built the Z80, igniting the eight-bit personal computer era. For AI the significance was never raw speed but the premise that computing could be packaged, sold, and fitted into anything; PCs, embedded systems, robots, GPUs, and TPUs all rest on retailable compute elements.

timeline.title_zh: Prolog:逻辑编程语言问世
timeline.title_en: Prolog: First Logic Programming Language
timeline.summary_zh:
1972 年,Alain Colmerauer 和 Philippe Roussel 在马赛大学(Luminy)设计出 Prolog(Programmation en Logique)。
Robert Kowalski 同期在爱丁堡给出 SLD 反驳消解的理论基础,即“算法 = 逻辑 + 控制”。
Prolog 把程序员的角色改成两件事:写事实,写规则,机器自己用反演推理找答案。
1977 年 Warren 在爱丁堡实现首个 Prolog 编译器(DEC-10 Prolog);1983 年又设计了 Warren 抽象机(WAM),成为日后 Prolog 编译的事实标准,在 1980 年代成为欧洲 AI 和日本第五代计算机计划的核心语言。
timeline.source_name: Colmerauer, A. & Roussel, P. (1972); Kowalski, R. (1974) IFIP Congress
timeline.card_summary_zh: Prolog：逻辑编程语言问世；Prolog 让“声明式编程”和“逻辑推理引擎”进入主流。
timeline.summary_en: In 1972, Alain Colmerauer and Philippe Roussel designed Prolog (Programmation en Logique) at the University of Marseille (Luminy), while Robert Kowalski in Edinburgh established the theoretical foundation of SLD resolution refutation, "Algorithm = Logic + Control." The language shifted the programmer’s job to simply writing facts and rules, leaving the machine to find answers through deductive reasoning. In 1977, Warren implemented the first Prolog compiler (DEC-10 Prolog) in Edinburgh, later designing the Warren Abstract Machine (WAM) in 1983, which became the de facto compilation standard and the core language of European AI and Japan’s Fifth Generation Computer Systems project in the 1980s.
timeline.card_summary_en: Prolog brought declarative programming and logic inference engines into the mainstream.
timeline.why_it_matters_en: It shaped a generation of knowledge representation, expert systems, constraint solving, and natural-language interface design. Though no longer mainstream, Prolog's shadow persists in Datalog, SQL three-valued logic, rule engines, and graph-database query languages.
timeline.behind_scenes_en: Two streams converged into Prolog. Colmerauer was building a natural-language question-answerer and needed a tool handling yes, no, and list answers; Kowalski worked on automated theorem proving and Horn clause resolution. The two met through Marseille meetings in 1971 and 1972 and merged their lines. In 1982 Japan's Fifth Generation Computer project picked Prolog as its base language, making it the AI world's second language alongside LISP through the early 1980s.

timeline.title_zh: Lighthill 报告:英国 AI 第一次大裁员
timeline.title_en: Lighthill Report: AI General Survey
timeline.summary_zh:
1973 年,英国科学研究委员会(SRC)出版《Artificial Intelligence: a paper symposium》,卷首是 Sir James Lighthill 撰写的《Artificial Intelligence: A General Survey》。
Lighthill 把 AI 分成 A(高级自动化)、B(机器人等搭桥研究)、C(中枢神经系统的计算机模拟)。
他直接批评 A 类(定理证明)和 B 类(机器人)研究在“组合爆炸”面前束手无策,结论是“在所有领域,已取得的发现都没有产生当时承诺的重大影响”。
报告导致英国政府除爱丁堡、苏塞克斯、埃塞克斯三校外,停止对其他大学的 AI 研究资助,直接引发英国第一次 AI 寒冬。
timeline.source_name: Lighthill, J. (1973). Artificial Intelligence: A General Survey. SRC Paper Symposium
timeline.card_summary_zh: Lighthill 报告：英国 AI 第一次大裁员；Lighthill 报告是 AI 史上第一次“外部审计”触发寒冬的样本。
timeline.summary_en: In 1973, the British Science Research Council (SRC) published *Artificial Intelligence: a paper symposium*, opening with Sir James Lighthill’s *Artificial Intelligence: A General Survey*. Lighthill divided AI into Category A (advanced automation), Category B (bridge research like robotics), and Category C (computer simulation of the central nervous system), directly criticizing Category A (theorem proving) and Category B (robotics) as helpless against "combinatorial explosion." Concluding that "in no part of the field have the discoveries made so far produced the major impact that was then promised," the report led the British government to halt AI research funding for all universities except Edinburgh, Sussex, and Essex, directly triggering the UK's first AI winter.
timeline.card_summary_en: The Lighthill Report is AI history's first case of an outside audit triggering a winter.
timeline.why_it_matters_en: It showed AI is never only a technical matter; expectation management, funding structure, institutional politics, and press sentiment all decide survival. The winter talk and generative-AI bubble debates of 2023-2025 replay the same law: when promises go unredeemed, external review and policy tightening arrive together.
timeline.behind_scenes_en: The fuse had two layers. Technically, touring Edinburgh's machine intelligence department, Lighthill watched many demonstration systems collapse outside their little worlds and judged the gap between promise and reality too wide. Politically, Michie's long-running conflict with the sitting department head produced complaint letters to SRC, which wanted an external review to sort out where AI money went. The two forces together turned an internal assessment into the budget axe over British AI. Lighthill himself was no opponent of AI and later conceded parts of the report were too harsh.

timeline.title_zh: AARON:最早的长周期 AI 艺术系统
timeline.title_en: AARON: Early Long-Running AI Art System
timeline.summary_zh:
1973 年前后,英国艺术家 Harold Cohen 在加州大学圣地亚哥分校(UCSD)开始编写 AARON 绘画程序。
AARON 不是一次性生成器,而是 Cohen 用了 40 多年不断迭代的“合作者”。
早期版本(1970s)用规则在屏幕上画闭合轮廓与色块;1980 年代扩展到毛笔、岩石、植物造型;1990 年代加入色彩决策,程序能自己选颜色。
Cohen 后期让 AARON 直接驱动画布机械臂,真画物理水彩和丙烯。
timeline.source_name: Cohen, H. (1973-2010); Computer History Museum retrospective
timeline.card_summary_zh: AARON：最早的长周期 AI 艺术系统；AARON 把 AI 艺术史拉长到半个世纪。
timeline.summary_en: Around 1973, British artist Harold Cohen began writing the AARON painting program at the University of California, San Diego (UCSD), creating a "collaborator" he would iteratively develop for over 40 years rather than a simple one-off generator. While 1970s versions used rules to draw closed outlines and color blocks on screens, AARON expanded to brush, rock, and plant forms in the 1980s, and gained color decision-making in the 1990s to choose its own palette. Later on, Cohen had the program directly drive robotic arms to paint physical watercolors and acrylics onto canvas.
timeline.card_summary_en: AARON stretches AI art history across half a century.
timeline.why_it_matters_en: Anyone debating today whether AI can be an artist finds in AARON that the tangle of tools, rules, randomness, and authorship is a long-running question of AI art, not something newly invented in 2022.
timeline.behind_scenes_en: Discussion of AI art defaults to DALL-E or diffusion models, but AARON pushes the line back fifty years. Cohen's core question was never whether a machine can draw but how authorship divides. He consistently refused to call AARON an independent artist, insisting on final attribution rights himself, a question that returned as a legal and ethical focus in the generative AI era.

timeline.title_zh: WABOT-1:第一台全尺寸人形机器人
timeline.title_en: WABOT-1: First Full-Scale Humanoid Robot
timeline.summary_zh:
1973 年,早稻田大学加藤一郎实验室完成 WABOT-1(WAseda roBOT 1)。
它身高 1.6 米,重 130 公斤,由四个子系统组成:WAMOT-1(机械臂,5 自由度 + 抓持)、WL-5(下肢,液压驱动,静步态行走)、视觉系统(接触 / 触觉 / 简易距离感)、语音系统(简单元音识别和合成)。
走一步大约 45 秒,但能自主完成“看 - 走 - 抓 - 简单对话”闭环。
timeline.source_name: Kato, I. (1973). Waseda Univ. Bioengineering Lab report; humanoid.waseda.ac.jp
timeline.card_summary_zh: 早稻田大学加藤一郎实验室完成 WABOT-1(WAseda roBOT 1)；WABOT-1 是具身智能史的第一座里程碑。
timeline.summary_en: In 1973, Ichiro Kato’s laboratory at Waseda University completed WABOT-1 (WAseda roBOT 1). Standing 1.6 meters tall and weighing 130 kilograms, it was composed of four subsystems: WAMOT-1 (a robotic arm with 5 degrees of freedom and gripping), WL-5 (hydraulically driven lower limbs for static gait walking), a vision system (contact, tactile, and simple distance sensing), and a voice system (simple vowel recognition and synthesis). Although it took about 45 seconds to take a single step, it could autonomously complete the closed loop of "seeing, walking, grasping, and simple conversation."
timeline.card_summary_en: Waseda University's Kato laboratory completed WABOT-1, embodied intelligence's first milestone.
timeline.why_it_matters_en: WABOT-1 moved AI out of on-screen conversation into a body in a real room, instantly exposing fresh problems stacked from intelligence plus gravity plus friction plus sensing delay. The technical trees of Honda ASIMO, Boston Dynamics Atlas, and Tesla Optimus all hold early prototypes inside WABOT-1's subsystems.
timeline.behind_scenes_en: The hard part was not walking but not falling. It used a static gait, shifting its center of gravity over the support foot before lifting the other, with pressure sensors underfoot reporting weight position in real time. Driven by relays and hydraulics it was enormous and power-hungry, and 1973 compute could not attempt real-time dynamic balance, so Kato's team used mechanical engineering and physiology to simplify the problem until a machine could run it.

timeline.title_zh: Xerox Alto:第一台图形界面个人计算机
timeline.title_en: Xerox Alto: First GUI Personal Computer
timeline.summary_zh:
1973 年 3 月 1 日,Xerox PARC 的 Alto 计算机首次运行。
由 Butler Lampson 提案(1972 年 12 月备忘录),Chuck Thacker 主导硬件设计,Robert Metcalfe 与 David Boggs 发明以太网。
Alto 把“位图显示 + 鼠标 + 三键 + 窗口 + WYSIWYG 文档 + 局域网 + 激光打印机”整合到一台机器里。
这是 Steve Jobs 1979 年参观 PARC 看到的“未来”,直接催生 Apple Lisa 和 Macintosh。
timeline.source_name: Thacker, C. et al. (1979) Xerox Alto; Turing Award 2009
timeline.card_summary_zh: Xerox PARC 的 Alto 计算机首次运行；Alto 决定了今天所有个人计算设备的视觉和交互范式。
timeline.summary_en: On March 1, 1973, Xerox PARC’s Alto computer ran for the first time; proposed in a December 1972 memo by Butler Lampson, its hardware design was led by Chuck Thacker, while Robert Metcalfe and David Boggs invented Ethernet. The Alto integrated a bitmap display, a mouse, three buttons, windows, WYSIWYG documents, a local area network, and a laser printer into a single machine. This was the "future" Steve Jobs saw during his 1979 visit to PARC, directly spawning the Apple Lisa and Macintosh.
timeline.card_summary_en: Xerox PARC's Alto first ran, fixing the look and interaction of every personal device since.
timeline.why_it_matters_en: Alto decided the visual and interaction paradigm of personal computing today. For AI, graphics plus mouse moved conversing with machines from command-line specialists to everyone, preparing the user base for MATLAB, Jupyter, and AI toolchains on PCs. Thacker received the 2009 Turing Award for the Alto design.
timeline.behind_scenes_en: Each Alto cost 12,000 dollars and PARC built roughly 2,000, but Xerox executives never commercialized it, reasoning that personal computers had no market. When Jobs brought the Apple team through PARC in 1979 and saw Smalltalk, Alto, bitmap editing, and overlapping windows, those ideas went home into the Lisa in 1983 and Macintosh in 1984, with Windows 1.0 continuing the Mac line in 1985. PARC invented the GUI; Apple and Microsoft made it a mass product.

timeline.title_zh: 第一次 AI 寒冬:英美同步降温
timeline.title_en: First AI Winter Begins
timeline.summary_zh:
1973-1974 年,英美 AI 经费同步大砍,构成第一次 AI 寒冬。
英国:Lighthill 报告(1973)导致 SRC 停止对爱丁堡之外多数大学的 AI 资助。
美国:DARPA 1969 年 Mansfield 修正案后必须证明项目“直接军事相关”,1971-1974 年大幅削减 CMU、MIT、SRI、斯坦福的 AI 通用研究经费,1974 年的 DARPA AI 研究预算比 1968 年下降约 30%。
学术界:Minsky 与 Papert《Perceptrons》(1969)被误读为“神经网络已死”,连接主义研究在 70 年代几乎断流。
timeline.source_name: Crevier, G. (1993). AI: The Tumultuous History; McCorduck 2004; Russell & Norvig 3rd ed.
timeline.card_summary_zh: 承诺远超实际能力后，英美资助机构同时收紧经费，AI 第一次为过度乐观付出整个行业的代价。
timeline.summary_en: The first AI winter set in during 1973–1974 as the UK and US simultaneously slashed funding: the UK’s Lighthill Report (1973) led the SRC to halt AI funding for most universities except Edinburgh. In the US, the 1969 Mansfield Amendment required projects to be "directly military-related," prompting DARPA to drastically cut general AI research funding at CMU, MIT, SRI, and Stanford between 1971 and 1974, leaving the agency's 1974 AI budget down about 30% compared to 1968. Meanwhile, in academia, Minsky and Papert’s *Perceptrons* (1969) was misread as declaring "neural networks are dead," causing connectionist research to almost completely dry up in the 1970s.
timeline.card_summary_en: With promises far past capability, British and American funders cut at once, billing all of AI.
timeline.why_it_matters_en: The first winter is AI history's most complete promise-reality-punishment loop. Understanding it explains why sticking with neural networks in the 1990s made Hinton and LeCun look stubborn beyond reason, and where the dread in post-2023 bubble talk originates. AI's history is never one-way progress but cycles of overheating, winter, and recovery.
timeline.behind_scenes_en: The winter was three forces stacked. Technical: machine translation, machine vision, and speech recognition missed 1960s promises, and combinatorial explosion stalled general problem solvers on real tasks. Economic: the 1973 oil shock and US recession squeezed government research budgets everywhere. Institutional: DARPA stopped tolerating pure scientific curiosity and demanded deliverable military value. Pressed together, they demoted AI from tomorrow's star to over-promising failure; students stopped enrolling, professors switched fields, and the cold lasted until expert systems revived things in 1980.

timeline.title_zh: Minsky 框架理论:知识表示的新结构
timeline.title_en: Minsky Frames: A Framework for Representing Knowledge
timeline.summary_zh:
1974 年 6 月,Marvin Minsky 在 MIT AI Lab Memo 306 发表《A Framework for Representing Knowledge》,1975 年收录进 Winston 编辑的《The Psychology of Computer Vision》。
论文提出“框架(Frame)”数据结构:一个框架描述一类刻板场景(如“走进客厅”),顶部是固定信息,底部是若干“槽(slot)”装具体实例,槽有默认值,可被子框架覆盖。
框架之间组成“框架系统”,通过变换表示视角、动作和因果关系。
timeline.source_name: Minsky, M. (1974). MIT-AI Memo 306; (1975) in Winston (ed.) Psychology of Computer Vision
timeline.card_summary_zh: 框架理论用槽位和默认值组织场景知识，为机器表示人物、物体、动作和因果关系提供了新结构。
timeline.summary_en: In June 1974, Marvin Minsky published "A Framework for Representing Knowledge" as MIT AI Lab Memo 306, which was later included in the 1975 book *The Psychology of Computer Vision* edited by Winston. The paper proposed the "Frame" data structure to describe stereotyped scenarios (like "entering a living room"), utilizing fixed information at the top and "slots" for specific instances at the bottom, which have default values that subframes can override. Together, these frames form a "frame system" that uses transformations to represent perspectives, actions, and causal relationships.
timeline.card_summary_en: Slot-and-default frames gave machines a new structure for scenes, objects, actions, and causes.
timeline.why_it_matters_en: Frames were the turning point in symbolic knowledge representation, upgrading atomic propositions plus predicate logic into composite structures carrying defaults, laying conceptual groundwork for the 1980s expert-system boom. Object-oriented programming, JSON Schema, Protobuf messages, and vector database schemas all bear Frame's imprint.
timeline.behind_scenes_en: The real contribution was less a data structure than defaults plus perspective shifting: Minsky wanted frames to explain how you know a living room probably holds a sofa before surveying the room. The paper itself admitted it poses a series of questions more than it supplies answers.
